articles.title: Fresh New York Yankees Playoff Predictions, Player Stat Projections For Final Month
articles.summary: The New York Yankees took three out of four in a pivotal series with the Boston Red Sox this past weekend, opening up a four-game lead over those loathed rivals in the race for the American League's top wild card spot.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees took three out of four in a pivotal series with the Boston Red Sox this past weekend, opening up a four-game lead over those loathed rivals in the race for the American League's top wild card spot.

At 4.5 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for the No. 1 seed, though, the Yankees are still hoping for more with four weeks remaining until the finish line.

How will things play out for the Bronx Bombers in September?

More importantly, how are they shaping up for October?

We'll start out with some key injury updates before diving into updated projections for the Yankees for the closing stretch.

Before Sunday's series finale against the Red Sox, Yankees manager Aaron Boone told reporters that Aaron Judge (rib) will travel with the team on the upcoming West Coast road trip, with the intention of increasing his pregame activities. Though there has been no indication yet that he could play this week against the Angels or Padres, Judge has said that he ideally will return without going on a rehab assignment. At this point, we're just kind of waiting to see when he shows up in the lineup. He could return during next week's homestand.

George Lombard Jr. (knee) is considered day-to-day after tweaking his knee on a checked swing and leaving two innings later during the second game of Saturday's doubleheader. He did not play on Sunday. ﻿

Ryan McMahon (thumb) played in a rehab game on Saturday and will likely return on Tuesday, when rosters expand from 26 to 28.

Clarke Schmidt (Tommy John) began a rehab assignment on Saturday. In 20 pitches, he allowed a triple and a home run while striking out two batters. There's still hope he returns in mid-September, though he would almost certainly do so in a relief capacity.

For the first time this season, the Yankees have their ideal postseason starting rotation intact.

Gerrit Cole tossed a quality start on Thursday. Cam Schlittler went 5.2 scoreless innings on Friday. And though both Carlos Rodón and Max Fried were on a pitch count for Saturday's doubleheader, the former threw 88 pitches in Game 1 and the latter tallied 63 pitches in the nightcap.

What should we expect from each down the stretch, in what should be five remaining starts apiece?

Gerrit Cole already has been hot as of late, boasting a 2.57 ERA over his last nine appearances, eight of which were quality starts. But if the rotation holds to form, his next three starts would come against the Angels, Rockies and Mets. He might do some serious shoving in September. We'll pencil him in for 32 IP, a 2.25 ERA and 37 strikeouts.

Naturally, we expect big things from Cam Schlittler , who is in quite the two-horse race with Dylan Cease for the AL Cy Young. He has struggled with his control recently, though, issuing 16 walks in his last five starts after allowing just 26 in his first 23 outings. He'll reel it back in for September, helped by matchups with the Angels and Rockies in his next two starts. It might be lazy, but we're putting him down for the same projection of 32 IP, 2.25 ERA and 37 K. (And, yes, he wins the Cy Young.)

With both Carlos Rodón and Max Fried , the priority is simple: Stay healthy. Each has made two IL trips this season and is still building back up from the latest.

Both have been solid when available, though. Fried has a 2.80 ERA for the year, while Rodón is at a 2.82 ERA over his last 10 starts.

Rodón goes 26.2 innings across his remaining five starts with a 3.37 ERA and 25 strikeouts. Fried gives them 25.0 innings with a 2.88 ERA and 20 strikeouts.

Lastly, Paul Blackburn has suddenly become the go-to guy in pivotal situations prior to the ninth inning, both because he hasn't allowed an earned run across his last 15 appearances and because Fernando Cruz is done for the year. If he continues compiling holds while the big four starters remain healthy, it's going to be hard to pick against the Yankees, at least until the World Series.

However, Blackburn—whose 1.62 ERA is at odds with a 3.44 xERA, 3.62 FIP and 3.85 xFIP—comes back to earth a bit down the stretch with a 4.00 ERA and two blown saves in September.

Prior to that 16-1 shellacking of Boston on Sunday, the Yankees had averaged 3.53 runs across their previous 64 games, ranking nearly dead last in the majors since mid-June.

At least in terms of batting average, their three best hitters during that 2.5-month stretch were someone they traded for (Luis García Jr., .309), a player who made his MLB debut in early August (George Lombard Jr., .253) and the guy who got demoted when they promoted Lombard (Anthony Volpe, .239).

Are the bats going to sputter through September, too? Or will a favorable remaining schedule—of their eight remaining opponents, six rank in the bottom half of the majors in run prevention—help them right the ship?

Here's what Steamer projects for the rest of the season for seven of New York's most important position players, and whether we agree with the forecast:

Ben Rice : .242/.334/.478, 6 HR, 14 RBI—Rice has been all over the map this season; an MVP-caliber hitter in April, May and July, but a bench-caliber hitter in June and August. So, who knows what September holds? But he's five home runs away from 40 and could even end up being the reason Yordan Alvarez fails to complete the Triple Crown.

Cody Bellinger : .259/.332/.439, 4 HR, 15 RBI, 2 SB—In 38 games played since June 17, Bellinger has one home run and an OPS of .564. If he goes for four and .771, respectively, that could be what turns this entire offense around. And our guess is that he does finish relatively strong, maybe even a bit better than this projection.

Jazz Chisholm Jr. : .231/.314/.420, 4 HR, 11 RBI, 6 SB—September has historically been Chisholm's least productive month. (Well, actually, October has been.) However, if ever there was a year for him to finish strong, it's this one, to springboard into free agency on a high note. And over his last 12 games, he's batting .384 with eight stolen bases. He likely won't stay that hot, but he will at least surpass this stolen-base projection.

Luis García Jr. : .270/.312/.481, 4 HR, 12 RBI, 2 SB—García had an .873 OPS with the Nationals before the trade deadline and he has had an .884 OPS with the Yankees. Why the sudden dip to a sub-.800 projection, especially considering they can platoon him with Paul Goldschmidt to pretty much avoid left-handed starting pitchers the rest of the way? He should fare a bit better than this.

Heliot Ramos : .246/.313/.418, 3 HR, 11 RBI—Ramos finally broke through with a home run on Sunday, but he entered the day batting .119 in his 20 games with the Yankees. Factor in his final 22 games with the Giants and we're talking a 42-game stretch with a .518 OPS. This projection feels way too generous, as once Judge is able to return, Ramos is probably out of a job.

George Lombard Jr. : .223/.309/.349, 2 HR, 9 RBI, 2 SB—With the obvious exception of Judge's health, arguably the biggest X-factor for the Yankees in September is shortstop. If this is what Lombard hits, does he even keep the job? Or does his erratic glove become such a problem that they pivot back to Anthony Volpe just before the finish line? Either way, this projection reflects what he has shown thus far in the majors and is probably close to what actually happens.

Aaron Judge (6 games) : .274/.409/.560, 2 HR, 5 RBI—When Judge returned from nearly two months on the IL in 2023, he had a .965 OPS and homered in one out of three games played the rest of the way. Steamer is projecting basically a carbon copy of that here, which seems fair. However, six games is mighty pessimistic. Sixteen games feels more realistic.

In last week's projections , we had the Yankees securing the No. 4 seed and the Wild Card Series home-field advantage that comes with it, but getting bounced immediately by then-red-hot Boston.

But after the Yankees took three out of four (two of them in blowout fashion) against the Red Sox, we're changing our tune here.

For the second consecutive year, New York knocks out Boston in Game 3 of the Wild Card Round.

And instead of turning around and losing to the AL East winner in the ALDS, they're also going to topple Tampa Bay in four games before possibly sweeping whoever is left standing from the AL Central/West in the ALCS.

With the pitching staff healthier than it has been all season and Judge hopefully nearing a return of his own, this team's ceiling feels as high as it has in nearly three months.

Is it high enough to take down the Dodgers in the World Series? Well, maybe not. But a repeat of the 2024 World Series matchup sure would be a fun final hurrah before the impending lockout.

articles.title: Brian Cashman Addresses Yankees Contract and Future amid MLB World Series Pursuit
articles.summary: New York Yankees longtime general manager Brian Cashman's contract is set to end after the 2026 season, but he's not worried about his future.
articles.body:
New York Yankees longtime general manager Brian Cashman's contract is set to end after the 2026 season, but he's not worried about his future.

The Athletic's Ian O'Connor reported that Cashman "is expected to sign yet another deal" with the Yankees after this year, and the GM chose not to address his contract status while speaking to reporters on Sunday.

"I like how Jazz (Chisholm Jr.) answered it. He's a free agent at the end of the year too, and he just said he wants to win the World Series and nothing else really matters," Cashman said. "My contract is for another day. It's not something I control or am thinking about. I'm very honored to be a part of this franchise as long as I have, but right now all I'm focused on is figuring out how to win this thing."

articles.title: Yankees’ Austin Wells makes MLB history, becomes first player to accomplish feat
articles.summary: The Yankees catcher made MLB history in Sunday's victory over the Red Sox.
articles.body:
On Sunday afternoon, the New York Yankees defeated the Boston Red Sox by a score of 16-1. The game gave the Yankees the series win and the season series win, which could be huge come MLB playoff time. If the two teams finish the season tied, the Yankees now own the tiebreaker. That wasn't the only story, though.

The game results on Sunday were exciting, but it's what Austin Wells did during the game that made history. Perhaps it is the type of performance that can change the fortunes of his season, too.

Oct 1, 2025; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees catcher Austin Wells (28) celebrates his go ahead RBI single against the Boston Red Sox during the eighth inning of game two of the Wildcard round of the 2025 MLB playoffs at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images

There are times when pinch hitters make a massive impact on the game in one inning, but no player has come in and launched two balls over the wall in the same inning. Sunday, Austin Wells hit two home runs in the contest versus the Boston Red Sox and became the first player in MLB history to hit two home runs in the same inning as a pinch hitter.

The Yankees rallied that entire inning, scoring 8 runs in the bottom of the 8th to seal the series against the Boston Red Sox.

Can Austin Wells turn his season around?

May 3, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees catcher Austin Wells (28) at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images

Austin Wells has been criticized for his lack of offense on this team, but over his last 10 games, the Yankees catcher is hitting .269 and has 9 RBIs. Since July 9th, he is slashing .250 with 25 hits and 16 RBIs.

The big question for Wells has always been the offense. He is currently batting .184 on the season with an OPS of .593. Recently, the bat has picked up, but one thing that Yankee fans wanted was to upgrade at catcher for better offense.

He is one of the best framers in the league and knows the strike zone. Wells is 3rd in the MLB in successful overturns with 68. Only William Contreras of the Milwaukee Brewers and Tyler Stephenson of the Cincinnati Reds have higher percentages.

Wells can still be a good hitter and has shown better at-bats through this recent stretch. He is going to be the starting playoff catcher, barring any injury, so Austin Wells still has a great opportunity to turn his year around.

articles.title: Red Sox radio broadcaster Will Flemming says team should hit Austin Wells, calls Jazz Chisholm a 'bush-league player' in meltdown
articles.summary: Jazz Chisholm found a way to get under the skin of multiple Red Sox broadcasters Sunday.
articles.body:
It was a highly-productive weekend for the New York Yankees, who took three out of four games from the rival Boston Red Sox. Of those wins, Sunday's 16-1 victory proved to be the most embarrassing for Boston … and not just on the field.

During the contest, Red Sox radio announcer Will Flemming openly advocated for the team to hit Yankees catcher Austin Wells with a pitch and referred to Jazz Chisholm as a "bush-league player" after Chisholm stole two bases with the Yankees up six runs.

Flemming's disgust started after Chisholm stole second and third with the Yankees up 7-1 in the bottom of the eighth. Chisholm stole the bases on consecutive pitches, leading Flemming to suggest the Red Sox throw at Wells, who was at the plate.

Flemming also said "[Chisholm] is a bush-league player, that the pitcher "should fight" Chisholm and that Chisholm "plays the game the wrong way."

Former Red Sox third baseman Will Middlebrooks — who was on the broadcast with Flemming — gave his thoughts on the matter, saying the Red Sox weren't holding Chisholm on the base, which was a "white flag," meaning the team had given up on the game. Middlebrooks later called Chisholm's steals a "selfish play."

The Yankees opened things up in a major way after Chisholm's steals. Wells hit a two-run shot to right field, scoring Chisholm from third. Paul Goldschmidt followed that up with a home run of his own.

The team later added six more runs in the frame, as Wells hit a second home run during the inning.

Flemming wasn't the only Red Sox broadcaster to show ire about Chisholm's steals. Lou Merloni, who provides color commentary on NESN, said he had " a problem with [Chisholm stealing.] " Merloni echoed Middlebrooks' comments, saying it was bad form for Chisholm to steal in that situation.

Merloni didn't go nearly as far as Flemming, though did add in a "Red Sox didn't do much about [Chisholm's steals]. Wells was still at the plate." That's not the same as advocating for the team to hit Wells, but Merloni at least seemed to think the team could have considered it in that instance.

Given the score of Sunday's game — and the Red Sox's performance the entire series — Flemming and Merloni's comments come off as sour grapes after the Yankees got the best of their biggest rivals.

Following those wins, the Yankees hold a four-game lead over the Red Sox in the American League East. Both teams, however, are firmly in the wild-card hunt.

That could set up a future playoff series … one in which the Red Sox will have to determine how important it is to send a message if their season is on the line.

articles.title: Red Sox Broadcaster Blasts Jazz Chisholm Jr. as 'Bush League,' Wonders If SP Should Hit Yankees Star
articles.summary: A Boston Red Sox radio play-by-play announcer crossed the line in his criticism of New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. during Sunday's 16-1 loss.
articles.body:
A Boston Red Sox radio play-by-play announcer crossed the line in his criticism of New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. during Sunday's 16-1 loss.

Per ESPN , after Chisholm stole second and third base while the Yankees were holding a 7-1 lead, WEEI's Will Flemming called the two-time All-Star a "bush league player" and suggested that Red Sox left-handed reliever Jovani Moran should "drill" one of his teammates.

Flemming took to social media on Monday to apologize for his comments:

New York Knicks star Josh Hart—a known Yankees fan—had some critical messages toward Flemming:

Chisholm drew a leadoff walk against Moran to start the eighth inning and promptly stole second base. Since he wasn't being held at second, he quickly stole third base without a throw, at which point Flemming and WEEI color analyst Will Middlebrooks began their criticism.

"Chisholm's doing it again," Flemming said as Chisholm stole third. "This is what he does."

While Middlebrooks lamented about Chisholm stealing an extra base, Flemming added that Moran should retaliate against Yankees catcher Austin Wells.

"Wouldn't you sort of like to see Moran drill Wells right here?" he said.

Middlebrooks didn't address that suggestion and responded that Chisholm was being "selfish" and "padding your stats," while Flemming added that the 28-year-old "is a bush league player." Wells later launched a two-run home run off Moran, and Chisholm's slow trot to home plate angered Flemming even more.

"Moran should fight Chisholm," Flemming said. "[Moran] is walking toward the third-base line, staring at him there."

The Red Sox (74-63) are now four games behind the Yankees (78-59) in the AL Wild Card race, and they officially lost the season series against New York. Flemming said he feels the situation likely added "a little extra vinegar" to a potential postseason series between the longtime rivals before once again turning his attention to Chisholm.

"I'm gonna say it, he plays the game the wrong way," he said, though he later added that Chisholm is "awesome" and "so talented."

articles.title: Ketel Marte Will Rejoin D-Backs for Phillies Series After Stints on Injured, Restricted Lists
articles.summary: The Arizona Diamondbacks are activating three-time All-Star Ketel Marte, according to MLB insider Francys Romero and the New York Post's Jon Heyman.
articles.body:
The Arizona Diamondbacks are activating three-time All-Star Ketel Marte, according to MLB insider Francys Romero and the New York Post 's Jon Heyman .

Marte hasn't suited up for Arizona since a 5-3 loss to the Atlanta Braves on Aug. 16.

The Diamondbacks are opening a three-game series against the Philadelphia Phillies on Monday.

They initially placed Marte on the restricted list after he failed to report at Fenway Park prior to their series opener with the Boston Red Sox on Aug. 17.

"It's been a crazy day," manager Torey Lovullo told reporters at the time. "All I know is that he's dealing with a personal issue. We're trying to figure that out, and he didn't show up today and he was put on the restricted list. That's as much as I know right now. I just was doing my best to reach out to him, and there was very little coming back."

Marte's agent, Charisse Espinosa-Dash, said two days later he was also dealing with a knee issue, with Arizona shifting him to the 10-day injured list.

The story took another turn when fans spotted the veteran infielder at the Talking Stick Resort casino. Lovullo downplayed the significance because Marte had been doing his required work at the Diamondbacks' training facility in Scottsdale.

The Diamondbacks are second in the National League West at 73-65. While they're unlikely to catch the Los Angeles Dodgers and win the division, they have a half-game cushion on the San Diego Padres for the final wild-card spot.

A healthy Marte could help Arizona secure a playoff berth, though his 2026 performance has been below his usual standards. He has a .249/.314/.446 slash line and 21 home runs through 118 games.

articles.title: Luis Robert Jr. Landing Spot Revealed After Mets Waived Outfielder Ahead of MLB Roster Deadline
articles.summary: The Baltimore Orioles claimed outfielder Luis Robert Jr. after the New York Mets placed him on outright waivers Sunday.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Orioles claimed outfielder Luis Robert Jr. after the New York Mets placed him on outright waivers Sunday.

Chelsea Janes of SNY first reported the news.

By adding Robert prior to the Sept. 1 roster deadline, he will be eligible to play in the postseason should Baltimore qualify.

The Mets will also up outfield prospect Nick Morabito, per Will Sammon of The Athletic. He's posted 13 homers, 47 RBI, 42 stolen bases and a .743 OPS in Triple-A this season.

New York traded infielder Luisangel Acuna and right-hander Truman Pauley for Robert in January, but it was among the moves that didn't pan out for the cellar-dwelling Mets (61-76). The veteran center fielder is hitting just .223 with 10 homers, 23 RBI, 24 runs and a .702 OPS this season, numbers that have been seriously bolstered by a hot month of August (.841 OPS, six homers, 11 RBI).

That hot streak came after he received little interest ahead of the trade deadline, and was perhaps enough reason for the Orioles to claim him on waivers.

Baltimore, meanwhile, has clawed its way back into playoff contention after winning seven of its past nine. That has left the Orioles just one game back of the Cleveland Guardians for the final AL Wild Card berth. Should they surpass the Guardians, the AL East would have four teams in playoff position.

Adding a right-handed hitter in the outfield made sense for an Orioles team rolling with a starting group of Colton Cowser, Dylan Beavers (both lefties) and Leody Taveras (a switch-hitter who has posted a .518 OPS against left-handed pitchers).

Cowser has been even worse against lefties (.482 OPS), while Beavers has been somewhat more respectable in that regard but hardly effective (.600 OPS). Suffice to say, the Orioles had a need for a right-handed bat in the outfield.

If Robert stays hot, he'll offer a nice upgrade for the Orioles. At the very least, he'll give them an option to utilize against left-handed pitching if they go the platoon route.

articles.title: Phillies, White Sox Make Trade in New MLB Rumors Ahead of Playoff Roster Eligibility Deadline
articles.summary: The Chicago White Sox added some veteran help ahead of Tuesday's playoff roster eligibility deadline.
articles.body:
The Chicago White Sox added some veteran help ahead of Tuesday's playoff roster eligibility deadline.

According to ESPN's Jeff Passan , the White Sox will acquire outfielder Tommy Pham from the Philadelphia Phillies, and he will join the team when rosters expand on Tuesday.

Chicago also acquired outfielder Jake Cave from the Tampa Bay Rays for cash, per the Tampa Bay Times ' Marc Topkin .

A longtime veteran who was drafted in 2006 before making his major-league debut in 2014, Pham started the 2026 campaign with the New York Mets after signing a minor-league contract in March. He was called up to the active roster the following month, but he went 0-for-13 with seven strikeouts in nine appearances before being designated for assignment and electing for free agency.

Pham then signed a minor-league deal with the Baltimore Orioles in May, but he never made it to the active roster before exercising the opt-out clause in his contract in June. He signed a minor-league contract with the Phillies later in the month. However, Philadelphia's talented outfield rotation left no room for the 38-year-old on the active roster.

After three straight years with less than 65 wins, the White Sox are entrenched atop the AL Central with a 72-64 record. With the team on the verge of its first playoff appearance since 2021, Chicago chose to take a chance on an experienced veteran as the stretch run of the regular season approaches.

The White Sox will open a four-game series against the Houston Astros (69-68) on Monday night.

articles.title: Texas learns the hard way not to mock Florida high school football, Lindsey Vonn stuns & USC's poor showing!
articles.summary: A Texas high school football team learned a brutal lesson after disrespecting Florida's St. Thomas Aquinas, trailing 38-0 by halftime Friday night.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com. Final day of August, folks. This is it. At 12:01, we officially begin the 'Ber months — otherwise known as the greatest stretch on the sports calendar. Forget sports ... it's the greatest stretch on the calendar, period. September. October. November. December. Four of the best months of the year, staring us right in our fat faces. How lucky are we? We got our college football appetizer on Saturday, and it starts in full this week. We get NFL next Wednesday (!!!). We have a three-day weekend coming up. Fantasy football drafts are in full swing. The WNBA is taking the next three weeks off. Again, who has it better than us? Labor Day, Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas. Unreal stretch coming up. Strap in and hold on tight. We're in for a wild little ride. Welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where a Texas high school football team learns the hard way not to disrespect the great state of Florida. This was never, ever going to end well. What else? I've got Lindsey Vonn smashing tennis balls and dominating in a green dress, my Red Sox got embarrassed over the weekend, and let's talk about that USC crowd from Saturday afternoon. It was pathetic, and for those screaming about it being a blowout Week 0 game, I've got some highlights out of South Dakota to show you. Give me a break. Grab you something tall and strong — but please don't make it a hurricane (we're entering PEAK time down here) — and settle in for a final-Monday-of-August 'Cap! This was a poor pregame decision Obviously, the end of August and beginning of the 'Ber months hit just a bit different down here in Florida. Case in point: We're currently spending the week monitoring 'Dolly,' which is, unfortunately, the next named storm on the list. Looks like we're just gonna get some possible rain remnants from her later this week, which is fine. Not the best, given it's rained all summer where I am, but better than the alternative. But it is a reminder that this is the time of year where the H-words really get active. This is a 'hold-your-breath' month for Floridians. Let's keep our heads down and eyes on the prize, folks. Let's GRIND. OK, let's get this class going by staying this great state and checking out last Friday's big national game between DeSoto (Texas) and St. Thomas Aquinas down in Fort Lauderdale: Give me a break, USC Hilarious. St. Thomas, by the way, has won seven straight state championships. They've been a Florida powerhouse since I was in school, and that was a long time ago. USC FOOTBALL RIPPED FOR PATHETIC CROWD AT HOME OPENER: 'ABSOLUTELY EMBARRASSING' There's always been this debate surrounding high school football ... which state produces the best talent? It's either Florida, Georgia, Texas or California. Those are the Big Four. I'd throw in Tennessee as well. Obviously, I'm biased. Duh. I live and breathe Florida. We have the greatest governor in the world, had no clue COVID was happening, and have so much leftover money in the budget we're about to nix property taxes (kinda). I played high school football down here. I covered it for years. I don't think it's particularly close. Don't poke the bear like that, DeSoto! Dumb decision. They went down, 38-0, in the first half and the second half took 15 minutes because there was a running clock. It Just Means More down here! You know where it doesn't mean more ... or, frankly, anything? Southern California: Jackrabbits, Lindsey & the Sox Goodness gracious. I know it was San Jose State, but come on. That's just pathetic. It was so bad, by the way, that USC felt the need to issue a STATEMENT on the attendance: "We understand the factors that impacted Saturday’s attendance," USC said, via USA Today. "We have high expectations and a premier home schedule this season, and we know the competitive advantage an electric Coliseum atmosphere can provide our program. We thank our fans who showed up Saturday and look forward to seeing increased attendance the rest of the season." Factors? What factors? The heat? It was 92 degrees. Give me a break. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE And no, I don't want to hear the "it was San Jose State!" argument. That's so weak. Guess who South Dakota State played on Saturday? articles.title: Why MLB contenders are getting players for nothing after the deadline
articles.summary: The Mets gave away a former All-Star for nothing. The Reds tried to give away two and got no takers. Here's how the waiver wire works.
articles.body:
Baseball spent the last three days running like Facebook marketplace.

Luis Robert Jr. sold. The Mets put the center fielder on waivers Saturday, essentially putting an ad out for the other 29 teams to let them know he was available. By Monday afternoon he was an Oriole. New York gets nothing back except salary relief and a waiver fee. No prospect, no draft pick, not even cash considerations. The Mets are just happy they are out from under the $3 million left on his deal.

Eugenio Suarez and TJ Friedl did not sell.

Cincinnati put both on waivers last week and told the other 29 teams they could have either one for the cost of their salary. Friedl's cost about $700,000. Nobody bit. He is still a Red, So is Suarez. And everybody knows the Reds were willing to give them away.

Nearly a month after MLB's official trade deadline, teams are looking for depth and potential at little cost and risk. They have been perusing the waiver wire like a marketplace for nearly a month. Monday was the last day that they could make a move and have it matter in October.

Ballpark vibes, big plays and wild celebrations during 2026 MLB season

Wait, didn't MLB say the trades were over Aug. 3?

They are. Since 2019 there has been no such thing as a trade after the deadline. MLB changed the trade deadline and eliminated the waiver trades in August 2019.

A waiver claim is not a trade. It's a giveaway with a receipt. A team puts a player on outright waivers, the other 29 teams are told he is available, and any of them can have him by agreeing to pay what is left on his contract. Nothing goes back to the original team beyond a $50,000 waiver fee.

No haggling. No prospects. Take him or leave him.

The worst team in baseball gets first dibs. Waiver priority runs in reverse of the standings, so the club with the uglier record picks first, and then if there are two really bad teams vying for a player, last season's record breaks ties.

Being bad is one of the few things baseball rewards immediately. But bad teams rarely make waiver claims.

These claims are also final. A team cannot float a player, see who bites and pull him back like they used to do. That loophole closed in 2019. Put him on waivers and he is gone if he is claimed.

A club going nowhere, like the Mets, is paying a veteran to finish out a lost month. Handing him to a team vying for a spot clears salary and opens the roster spot for somebody the team plans to keep.

It usually suits the player too. He gets a pennant race instead of a countdown to his offseason tee time.

Some claims are strategic. A contender can take a player it has no intention of using in order to keep him off a rival team.

He goes back to his locker, knowing the team was willing to give him away. And he is waiting for the other shoe to drop.

That's Suarez and Friedl right now. Unclaimed players stay put, and their teams can send them outright to the minors, though veterans with enough service time can refuse that and take free agency instead.

Why is there a flurry of moves on Aug. 31?

It's the last hours before the deadline that really matters.

To play in October, a player has to be in the organization before the Sept. 1 cutoff. MLB's rules draw the line on being on the 40-man roster or on the 60-day injured list. Players like Luis Robert Jr. and Tommy Pham, who was claimed by the White Sox from the Phillies , are eligible for October.

A claim takes about 48 hours to clear, so anyone hoping to dump salary had to file by the weekend. Saturday, Robert and Royals reliver John Schreiber were put on waivers. Monday, Robert is now an Oriole and Schreiber was claimed by the Yankees.

articles.title: Red Sox move Willson Contreras to IL with hamstring strain, amid boos from Boston fans for slow running
articles.summary: Contreras held his hand to his ear for louder boos, then got into a verbal exchange with a spectator at Fenway Park during an Aug. 19 game.
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox announced on Monday that leading home run hitter Willson Contreras is going on the 10-day injured list with a left hamstring strain .

Contreras, 34, has 26 home runs, 21 doubles and 79 RBI with a .274/.384/.516 slash average in 517 plate appearances in his first season with Boston. After playing at catcher for most of his MLB career, he transitioned to a full-time first baseman last season with the St. Louis Cardinals and that's where he's played with the Red Sox.

Going on the IL with a hamstring injury should settle what somehow became a contentious issue with some Red Sox fans in recent weeks. Twice in the past three weeks, Contreras was booed by fans at Fenway Park for not running hard to first base.

After receiving boos while jogging out a grounder to third base during a 7-6 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks on Aug. 19, Contreras channeled a professional wrestler and held his right hand to his ear to get a louder crowd reaction.

However, Contreras acknowledging the fan reaction didn't end there. In the bottom of the 10th inning, the 11-year veteran engaged with a spectator at the far end of the Red Sox dugout toward the outfield. Other Red Sox players, including Jarren Duran, became involved in the argument, according to MassLive's Chris Cotillo .

After the game ended, Contreras continued his exchange with the fan and eventually pointed him out to security. Asked about the incident afterwards, he downplayed it.

"He was inviting me to dinner," Contreras told reporters. "I was like, 'Nah, I'm good with it.'"

Earlier in the month, Contreras acknowledged he was dealing with a hamstring issue and talked to interim manager Chad Tracy about picking his spots for running hard during games.

When asked about the booing, Contreras said that fans had a right to express themselves and considered it part of playing baseball. Yet after the fan incident, he wanted people to understand that he wasn't 100% healthy.

"If you're a smart fan, you know what's going on," he said . "I'm not going to make any excuses because it's not an excuse. It's real. I just want to play through it. "It's just part of the game. I'm not gonna get hurt running on a ground ball," he added. "If you're a real fan and you know baseball, there's no case for me to hustle out of the box. I'm not 100%. My manager has my back. I talked to him and he gave me permission to do whatever it takes to take care of my legs."

"If you're a smart fan, you know what's going on," he said . "I'm not going to make any excuses because it's not an excuse. It's real. I just want to play through it.

"It's just part of the game. I'm not gonna get hurt running on a ground ball," he added. "If you're a real fan and you know baseball, there's no case for me to hustle out of the box. I'm not 100%. My manager has my back. I talked to him and he gave me permission to do whatever it takes to take care of my legs."

To fill Contreras' spot on the roster, catcher Mickey Gasper (.278 average, .840 OPS) was recalled from Triple-A Worcester, bouncing back up to the majors after being optioned when Roman Anthony and Trevor Story were activated from the IL before Sunday's 16-1 loss to the New York Yankees.

articles.title: Yankees' Cam Schlittler, CC Sabathia Rip Red Sox Broadcaster on IG for Jazz Chisholm Jr. Comments
articles.summary: Comments from a Boston Red Sox announcer do not seem to be sitting well with the New York Yankees.
articles.body:
Comments from a Boston Red Sox announcer do not seem to be sitting well with the New York Yankees.

Red Sox play-by-play announcer Will Flemming called Jazz Chisholm Jr. a "bush league player" and said Boston reliever Jovani Moran should "drill" one of his teammates during the Yankees' 16-1 win on Sunday, per ESPN .

Yankees legend CC Sabathia, current pitcher Cam Schlittler made their thoughts known about Flemming on Instagram , which mirrored those of New York Knicks guard Josh Hart:

Fleming took to social media amid the backlash and apologized while saying his comments "crossed a line" as he let his fandom become a factor during the broadcast:

The comments came after Chisholm drew a leadoff walk with New York holding a 7-1 lead. He proceeded to steal second and third base, which prompted Flemming to say he was "a bush league player" for taking the extra bases when the Yankees had a commanding advantage and Boston wasn't holding him on like it would have in a close game.

Yankees broadcaster Michael Kay reported that manager Aaron Boone initially told Chisholm not to steal. However, when the Red Sox opted not to hold Chisholm on at first base, Boone had Chisholm steal. With New York up by six runs, Boone was trying to gather additional insurance runs so he didn't have to potentially use David Bednar in relief.

Chisholm went 2-for-3 with three runs scored, two walks and two stolen bases, which brought his season-long total in the latter category to 40. If he gets one more stolen base this season, he will have a career-high.

The Yankees took three of four from the Red Sox and are now four games ahead of their rivals in the American League East race.

Both are in playoff position with Boston still a full five games ahead of the Cleveland Guardians in the race for the second wild-card spot.

The Yankees and Red Sox will not face each other again this season unless they meet in the playoffs.

articles.title: Ketel Marte Will Apologize to D-Backs, Addresses Casino Photo After Restricted, Injured List Stints
articles.summary: Ketel Marte is set to return to the Arizona Diamondbacks ahead of Monday's game against the Philadelphia Phillies after the team placed him on the restricted and then injured lists following his decision to not show up for a matchup with the Boston Red Sox.
articles.body:
Ketel Marte is set to return to the Arizona Diamondbacks ahead of Monday's game against the Philadelphia Phillies after the team placed him on the restricted and then injured lists following his decision to not show up for a matchup with the Boston Red Sox.

He told reporters he plans on apologizing to his teammates and added, "We're human, we all make mistakes."

Marte also said he woke up ahead of the game against the Red Sox in significant pain and was frustrated when he made the individual decision to skip it. He explained he has a positive relationship with Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo and let him down by not arriving.

The story remained in the headlines when Marte was seen in a casino when the Diamondbacks were playing, although Lovullo said at the time he was "free to do whatever he wants" if he put in the proper rehab work:

On Monday, Marte said he went to the casino on his "personal time."

Marte returning for Monday's game was the plan from the team's perspective.

Lovullo told reporters last Monday, "That's what we're thinking about. I think that will be the 10th day or the 11th day, so there is definitely a strategy to get him back on the field, get him healthy."

The manager also discussed the situation Monday:

Arizona placed Marte on the restricted list after he didn't show up to face the Red Sox but then made the decision to move him to the injured list because of inflammation in his left knee.

His return comes at an important time, as the Diamondbacks are a half-game ahead of the San Diego Padres for the final wild-card spot in the National League. They are also 4.5 games behind the Chicago Cubs and Phillies and have the opportunity to move up in the standings with the upcoming head-to-head matchups with Philadelphia.

Marte is slashing .249/.314/.446 with 21 home runs and 67 RBI in 118 games this season.

articles.title: Ketel Marte says he 'failed' Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo with absence; Lovullo declines to guarantee Marte won't go AWOL again
articles.summary: Marte declined to shed much light on his absence or offer a message to fans. Lovullo remains in his corner but confirmed this wasn't the first time Marte had...
articles.body:
For the first time since his unexplained absence for a game against the Boston Red Sox , Arizona Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte spoke about the situation with reporters on Monday.

Through an interpreter, he said that "I failed" manager Torey Lovullo. But he declined to shed much light on the absence that largely remains a mystery.

Marte addressed reporters prior to his team's home game against the Philadelphia Phillies. He was activated from the injured list and is back in the lineup for the first time since his Aug. 17 no-show for the game in Boston made headlines.

Marte spoke with reporters prior to addressing his teammates, with whom he had yet to speak since his mysterious absence.

"It's a moment of frustration," Marte said through an interpreter when asked what kept him from showing up to Fenway Park on Aug. 17. "I'm the type of person that when something's going on in my life, I don't like to talk about it. So that's kind of what was going on."

His unexpected absence that night left Lovullo struggling to explain what had happened.

"I'm sure in time we'll start to uncover and unravel some information," Lovullo told reporters that night. "But I knew that there was something going on today … I still believed he was going to be here. He just didn't show up."

The Diamondbacks placed Marte on the restricted list that night. Following an MRI, he was placed on the injured list due to knee inflammation.

On Monday, Marte acknowledged that he let Lovullo down and said his frustration had nothing to do with his manager.

"I get along really well with Torey," Marte said. "In that instance, I failed him by not showing up. That morning, I woke up, my body was in pain. I couldn't react. No one made the decision for me. I'm the one who made the decision to not show up."

Marte told reporters that he was feeling "very well" physically and mentally as of Monday and that he looked forward to addressing his teammates.

"I'm gonna stand in front of my teammates like a man," he said. "I don't want any of my teammates to go through what I went through that morning."

Beyond that, Marte did little to expound on what prompted his absence.

Marte acknowledges casino trip, declines to address fans

Marte acknowledged that he was at a casino in Arizona during a Diamondbacks home game while on the injured list. Multiple social media posts showed Marte gambling at the casino during Arizona's game against the Cincinnati Reds on Aug. 21.

"I've been injured before," he said of the casino trip. "Those are things that I do in my personal time."

When asked if he had a message for Diamondbacks fans, he shook his head no.

Lovullo has repeatedly been in Marte's corner during this ordeal, while acknowledging that this isn't the first time Marte has gone AWOL.

"It's not the first time," Lovullo confirmed Monday to reporters. "He's definitely a retreater. When things are on his mind, some things I cause when I crash down on him. I know you guys want me to sometimes bury him and make him feel even worse than he already does.

"He doesn't respond to that. But I feel like it's my job to do that sometimes. When I do it, he retreats. When something doesn't go well, he retreats. So this is not the first time."

One of the previous occasions in which Marte "retreated" was last season. He missed a midseason series against the St. Louis Cardinals to fly home to the Dominican Republic. He said afterward that he felt "frustrated" and was "in a bad spot" after his Arizona home got burglarized during the MLB All-Star break.

His absence reportedly caused a rift with his teammates and coaches as the All-Star second baseman was absent from a series in the midst of a playoff race. How his latest absence has impacted the Arizona clubhouse is unclear.

Lovullo: Report of 2023 Yankees absence 'pretty accurate'

Lovullo confirmed a recent report from Arizona Sports' John Gambadoro that Marte also no-showed for a game against the New York Yankees in 2023.

Per that report, Marte believed the game at Yankee Stadium would be postponed due to weather and stayed at the hotel instead of going to the ballpark. The game was played without Marte, and the Diamondbacks were in the midst of a playoff race.

"That article is pretty accurate," Lovullo said Monday.

Lovullo offers no guarantees about Marte moving forward

When asked, Lovullo declined to offer a guarantee that Marte won't go AWOL again.

"I don't," Lovullo said when asked if he has any guarantees. "The other times that it happened, I asked for it to never happen again. It's something that's a work in progress. I think he told you, he's human. He's not perfect. …

"This is as much progress as I've seen him make. He's communicating with you guys and with me as well. We talked about personality traits and different things like that, where normally he doesn't want to even talk about personality traits. 'Fastball, middle, homer, that's all I want to think about, OK?'"

Lovullo clarified that Marte told his manager that he won't go missing again.

"I want to believe what he says to me," Lovullo continued.

The Diamondbacks are in the midst of a playoff race. They entered Monday at 73-65, with a half-game lead over the San Diego Padres for the final wild-card spot in the National League.

Marte is a three-time All-Star who won NLCS MVP when the Diamondbacks made a surprise run to the World Series as the No. 6 seed in 2023. He's a career .278/.348/470 hitter and is in the midst of his fourth consecutive season with 20-plus home runs.

He has been the anchor of Arizona's lineup for years — when he shows up. The Diamondbacks are counting on him to be there in the midst of another playoff race. How the fans and his teammates receive him for the stretch run is yet to be seen.

articles.title: Cubs tag Brewers for franchise-record 9 HRs, break NL record for most HRs in a month
articles.summary: The hot-slugging Cubs didn't even need Pete Crow-Armstrong to join the party on Monday.
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs keep on slugging. On Monday, they didn't even need Pete Crow-Armstrong to join the party.

In a home game against the rival and MLB-best Milwaukee Brewers, the Cubs exploded for nine home runs in a 17-3 win . The home run tally set a franchise record for a single game. It fell one short of the single-game MLB record of 10 set by the Toronto Blue Jays in 1987.

It also capped a hot-slugging August for the Cubs, who have tallied 62 home runs since Aug. 1. That set a record for the most home runs in a calendar month by an NL team. Per MLB.com's Sarah Langs , it's the second-most home runs in a calendar month by one team in MLB history, trailing only the 2019 New York Yankees, who clobbered 74 in August.

Brewers starter Kyle Harrison caught the brunt of the damage Monday, with five home runs and nine earned runs allowed in 3 2/3 innings of a start that inflated his ERA from 2.79 to 3.45.

The Cubs got to Harrison early and often. Tyrone Taylor and Nico Hoerner notched back-to-back home runs in the bottom of the first inning, and the Cubs left the frame with a 4-0 lead.

Alex Bregman hit a home run in the second, then got to Harrison again in the fourth with a solo shot that extended Chicago's lead to 8-0.

Harrison faced three more batters before Brewers manager Paul Murphy went to the bullpen. But the starter wasn't the only Brewer to get battered.

By the time the Cubs had tallied 10 runs in the seventh inning, Milwaukee waved the white flag and stopped sending pitchers to the mound. First baseman Andrew Vaughn finished the game on the mound for the Brewers, recording the final six outs.

His high lobs over the plate surrendered three more home runs in the eighth. Bregman's third home run of the night capped the barrage with two outs in the bottom of the frame.

Vaughn finished the game with 7 earned runs allowed on 3 walks and 9 hits, including the 3 home runs. His ERA now stands at 30.00.

Crow-Armstrong — who totaled five home runs in Chicago's two previous games to bolster his MVP case — did not contribute to the cause on a 1-for-5 night at the plate. Instead, it was Bregman's three home runs that led the way; he was the only Cub who hit more than one.

Six other Cubs hitters got in on the action with a home run each. And the Wrigley Field stands remained packed when it was done, as fans celebrated with W flags and a joyous rendition of "Go Cubs Go" to mark the vanquishment of their NL Central rivals.

Chicago leaves Monday's win at 78-60, comfortably in control of an NL wild-card spot.

The Brewers, meanwhile, are fine. The pummeling by the Cubs counts for only one loss, and they leave Monday's defeat with baseball's best record intact at 85-53, seven games ahead of the Cubs in the division.

Milwaukee will have three more games to exact revenge in what they'll hope isn't a tide-turning four-game set in the race for the NL Central.

articles.title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. Responds to Red Sox Broadcaster's Comments, 'Not Going to Remember Who He Is'
articles.summary: Jazz Chisholm Jr. is paying no mind to the comments from a Boston Red Sox broadcaster who called the New York Yankees star a "bush league player."
articles.body:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. is paying no mind to the comments from a Boston Red Sox broadcaster who called the New York Yankees star a "bush league player."

Chisholm shrugged off Red Sox radio play-by-play broadcaster Will Flemming, who said he "plays the game the wrong way."

"I didn't even know who that was until this morning," Chisholm said of Flemming, per The Athletic's Chris Kirschner . "And I'm still not going to remember who he is after today."

Flemming criticized Chisholm after he stole two bases in the bottom of the eighth inning as the Yankees led 7-1. Flemming said that Red Sox left-handed reliever Jovani Moran should "drill" one of Chisholm's teammates for the move.

"They're called unwritten rules because you're not really breaking any rules," Chisholm said. "You've seen teams — actually them (last season) — do the same thing where they're pouring on runs. We didn't have nothing to say or nothing to do about it.

"That's just showing how unprofessional he is."

Flemming apologized for the comments on social media, admitting that he crossed the line.

Chisholm's decision to steal when the Red Sox weren't holding him on the bag came with a green light from manager Aaron Boone, who said he "did the right thing."

"I'm an old-school baseball guy," Boone said. "I've been around doing this forever. I respect some of the unwritten rules. I really do. I think they've evolved and changed some. At the end of the day, I've got to do what's right for my team and try not to get so caught up in what the other team's doing. I felt like we did the right thing."

The Yankees won the game 16-1, capping a 3-1 series win over their AL East rival.

articles.title: Max Scherzer's Strikeouts Make MLB History In Latest Blue Jays' 7-0 Win
articles.summary: Max Scherzer made MLB strikeout history during the Toronto Blue Jays’ 7-0 win over the Seattle Mariners on Sunday, August 30, 2026. Scherzer recorded ten str...
articles.body:
Max Scherzer made MLB strikeout history during the Toronto Blue Jays' 7-0 win over the Seattle Mariners on Sunday, August 30, 2026. Scherzer recorded ten strikeouts, moving into ninth place on MLB's all-time strikeout list. Scherzer's reemergence couldn't come at a better time for a struggling Blue Jays team.

Scherzer Moves To Ninth On MLB's All-Time Strikeout List

The Blue Jays wrapped up a three-game sweep of the Mariners on Sunday at the Rogers Center in Toronto, Canada, which included an ace-like outing from Scherzer. The veteran pitched seven strong innings, allowing only a single hit and a walk, topped off with ten strikeouts. The team is desperate for players to step up as they struggle to hit .500 and keep scrapping from outside the bubble for the final AL Wild Card spot.

How Many Career Strikeouts Does Max Scherzer Have?

Scherzer moved into the top ten MLB all-time strikeout leaders in a game against the Philadelphia Phillies earlier this year. Scherzer jumped another spot with his ten Ks on Sunday. By striking out Mariners catcher Cal Raleigh in the seventh inning, the veteran moved into ninth place with 3,535 career strikeouts, passing MLB Hall of Famer Gaylord Perry.

Scherzer realistically has a shot at finishing seventh in all-time strikeouts, with Detroit Tigers' Justin Verlander and MLB Hall of Famer Don Sutton in the way. Tom Seaver's sixth-place 3,640 Ks are likely out of reach, but Sutton has 3,574, while Verlander is currently on the 60-day IL with 3,554, just 20 more than the Blue Jay, a lofty but manageable goal.

After giving Scherzer a one-year, $15.5 million deal in 2025, the Blue Jays brought him back on a one-year, $3 million agreement. The first bumpy season continued into the current one, including a 6.16 ERA on the season after the game. That said, the 42-year-old has been finding his groove lately, as shown by a respectable 3.60 ERA over his last seven games, allowing just 14 ERs across that span.

Scherzer was injured and inconsistent for much of last season, finishing the regular season with 17 games played and a 5.19 ERA across 85 innings. The pitcher fought back to play a vital role in the Blue Jays' 2025 AL Championship, including 14.1 IP for a 3.77 ERA, playing an important cog in the Canadian postseason machine. Toronto finds themselves below projections currently, with disappointment on the verge of overflowing fans' minds. It'll be an uphill battle for the final AL Wild Card spot.

The Blue Jays both bought and sold significant pieces at the MLB Trade Deadline. Toronto shipped out household names like starting pitcher Kevin Gausman and outfielder Daulton Varsho, while acquiring players such as starting pitcher José Soriano and outfielder Brett Bateman. The team ultimately took a retooling approach. With mixed reactions from fans on the net-gain, the rebirth of a former Cy Young winner could be a substantial surge for a team struggling to find traction.

Max Scherzer's Career Accomplishments & Awards

Each spot Scherzer climbs in the chart is just another feather in the cap of a future first-ballot MLB Hall of Famer. The right-hander already has three Cy Youngs, two World Series Championships, and eight MLB All-Star nominations. He's also one of four pitchers to strike out 20 batters in a single nine-inning game, had two no-hitters in the same season, and three career immaculate innings.

The Blue Jays hope Scherzer's recent resurgence can help fuel another postseason run. They've slowly but steadily been climbing towards the final spot, but with so many mediocre teams in the mix, do the defending AL Champions have what it takes? With teams like the Cleveland Guardians, Baltimore Orioles, and Texas Rangers all realistically still in the mix, only time will tell.

articles.title: MLB Injury Report: Willson Contreras sidelined with hamstring strain, James Wood nearing return
articles.summary: Jorge Montanez breaks down all of the relevant injury news around the league over the last week.
articles.body:
In this week's Injury Report, the Red Sox lose Willson Contreras to a hamstring strain. The Nationals could be getting James Wood back on Tuesday. And Aaron Judge could be returning to the Yankees lineup sometime next week. All that and more as we highlight the most relevant injury news around the league this week.

⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peacock in 2026 ! In addition to becoming the exclusive home of Sunday Night Baseball, NBC Sports will broadcast MLB Sunday Leadoff, "Opening Day" and Labor Day primetime games, the first round of the MLB Draft, the entire Wild Card round of the postseason, and much more.

Contreras was pulled from Sunday's blowout loss to the Yankees with hamstring tightness. The Red Sox then placed him on the 10-day injured list on Monday with a left hamstring strain, an issue that Contreras has reportedly been dealing with for about a month. The 34-year-old first baseman will now get at least the next week and a half to rest. The hamstring issue can explain his August struggles, as he's hit .217 in the month. Mickey Gasper was recalled to take his place on the active roster and fill in at first base.

The Braves have won seven straight, PCA is surging toward MVP honors, and the Orioles are finally approaching .500.

Wood could be back in the Nationals lineup on Tuesday or Wednesday during a two-game set against the Braves. The 23-year-old star has been out since August 4 with a left oblique strain and took batting practice on Friday before playing seven innings and hitting a home run in a rehab game with Double-A Harrisburg on Sunday. Manager Blake Butera stated Wood would get Monday off before deciding when he'd be activated. There was some thought that Wood wouldn't need a rehab assignment, but he wanted to see some live pitching before returning. Meanwhile, keep an eye on Abram's status on Tuesday. He was scratched from Monday's lineup against Miami with back tightness, though it's thought to be precautionary.

Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Monday that Judge could be ready to return to the Yankees lineup during the team's next homestand, starting on Tuesday, September 8 against the Rockies. The 34-year-old star has been out of action since early June with a rib fracture. Despite the extended absence, it seems as though he'll bypass a minor league rehab assignment and join New York as soon as he's ready to return to game action.

Griffin may be ready to return from the injured list when first eligible on Friday for the team's series opener against the Angels. The 20-year-old shortstop started a minor league rehab assignment with Double-A Altoona on Sunday and went 1-for-3 while playing seven innings. He's been out of action since early July with a torn ligament in his left ring finger.

The Cardinals lost both starting middle infielders over the last week. Winn had sat out a handful of games with a thumb issue before he was diagnosed with a fracture that landed him on the 10-day injured list, retroactive to August 22. The 24-year-old shortstop has already been swinging a bat with significant improvement and could return as soon as Tuesday when first eligible. Meanwhile, Wetherholt was placed on the 10-day injured list on Sunday with right wrist tendinitis. There's no word on how much time he's expected to miss. The 23-year-old second baseman has enjoyed an excellent rookie campaign, slashing .242/.343/.370 with 17 homers, 88 runs scored, and 14 steals across 586 plate appearances.

Edwards was removed from Sunday's game against the Nationals after colliding with Jorbit Vivas on a slide into second base, leaving with thumb and elbow discomfort. He was diagnosed with a left thumb sprain and placed on the 10-day injured list on Friday. There's no timetable for a return, but the Marlins will certainly want to get him back quickly as long as they remain in the playoff hunt. The 27-year-old second baseman is having a strong season in Miami, hitting .282/.361/.376 with six homers and 20 steals over 137 games.

A groin issue for Hancock surfaced while making a diving play at first base against the Blue Jays on Friday, though he remained in the game, allowing five runs over five innings. The team then placed him on the 15-day injured list on Sunday with a left adductor strain, sidelining Hancock for at least the next two weeks. The Mariners had been operating with a six-man rotation, but could revert to a five-man while Hancock is unavailable. While he hasn't been quite as successful in the second half, he's still enjoyed a strong breakout season, posting a 3.57 ERA, 1.14 WHIP, and 126 strikeouts over 138 2/3 innings.

Buxton initially left last Tuesday's game against the Athletics with a re-aggravation of his hip injury. After sitting out three games, the team placed him on the 10-day injured list with a right hip impingement. Twins general manager Jeremy Zoll told reporters last week that the 32-year-old outfielder could be looking at offseason hip surgery, so there's a chance Buxton could be shut down if the Twins fall out of contention. Top prospect Walker Jenkins was recalled to take Buxton's place on the roster after hitting .308 with 12 homers and 17 steals across 69 games with Triple-A St. Paul.

Ryan is getting closer to a return to the Twins rotation. The 30-year-old right-hander is set to make a rehab start with Triple-A St. Paul on Tuesday and is aiming to get to around 50 pitches. He's been out of action since early August with a glute strain. Assuming he comes out of his rehab start feeling well, he could be in line to make the following start with the Twins.

Early, on the 60-day injured list with left elbow inflammation, is on track to begin a minor league rehab assignment on September 8. Out since late June with the elbow issue, there doesn't seem to be much chance of him giving the Nationals anything but a few shorter appearances if he's able to return at all before the end of the season.

articles.title: Chicago Cubs outslug Milwaukee Brewers in a 17-3 blowout win to cap National League record home run month
articles.summary: Alex Bregman started August without a three-home-run game in his baseball career. Amid a scorching stretch, Bregman ends the month with his lifetime total no...
articles.body:
Alex Bregman started August without a three-home-run game in his baseball career.

Amid a scorching stretch, Bregman ends the month with his lifetime total now sitting at two. He slugged his second three-home-run game within the last three weeks on Monday night, his latest capping a high-powered August for the Chicago Cubs.

The Cubs slugged a franchise record nine home runs in a 17-3 blowout win over the Milwaukee Brewers at Wrigley Field, putting an exclamation point on a stellar month of power production. They finished August with 62 home runs, second in MLB history dating to 1898 behind only the 2019 New York Yankees (74 in April) — and a new National League record for the most home runs in a calendar month.

Bregman is one of four Cubs to record multiple three-home-run games in a season, joining Aramis Ramírez (two in 2004), Sammy Sosa (three in 2001) and Dave Kingman (two in 1979).

"The quality of at-bat in the second half, it's been super consistent up and down the lineup, and it's been tough on opposing teams," Bregman said. "Guys are battling, knowing what kind of player they are, and putting together a really good at-bat. Overall, in general, a good start to the series. Once the clock hits midnight, it's a new day and get after it again tomorrow."

The Cubs (78-60) feasted on Brewers starter Kyle Harrison's fastball. Their first seven runs came off the lefty's heater, helping the Cubs build a 9-0 advantage through four innings. Tyrone Taylor (two-run HR), Nico Hoerner (solo HR) and Carson Kelly (RBI single) gave starter Clay Holmes a four-run lead to work with after the first inning. Then Bregman (two-run HR) added on in the second, and the runs kept coming in the fourth thanks to Seiya Suzuki (solo HR), another Bregman long ball (solo HR) and Miguel Amaya's bases-loaded walk.

The Brewers eventually turned to first baseman Andrew Vaughn to pitch for the final two innings, and the Cubs punished him, knocking in seven runs, including three home runs.

Holmes, meanwhile, cruised through six shutout innings with five hits and two walks allowed to accompany eight strikeouts. The muggy weather made it tough at times to get a good grip on his sinker, but he still managed to get 11 called strikes with the pitch and used it to finish off two of his strikeouts. In his last four starts, Holmes has surrendered just one run in 25 innings (0.36 ERA).

"You could kind of feel their energy," Holmes said of the offense. "After a couple series that we lost, you could tell that the position player group really wants to come out strong, and you can feel that. And just to be able to put a zero up there in the first and let them do their thing was nice. Especially pitching to a contact-oriented team and you have that lead, that makes that a little better."

Bregman and NL MVP front-runner Pete Crow-Armstrong became the first MLB teammates to combine for 25+ home runs, 25+ walks, 50+ RBIs and 50+ runs scored in a calendar month since the Yankees' Roger Maris and Mickey Mantle in July 1961, per OptaSTATS. They are also the first pair of teammates in Cubs history to each hit at least 12 home runs in a calendar month and the first teammate duo in MLB to accomplish the feat since the Texas Rangers' Rafael Palmeiro and Iván Rodríguez in August 1999.

"He is relentless," Cubs manager Craig Counsell said of Bregman. "In his preparation and in the daily grind, he's just relentless."

Monday kickstarted a 10-day stretch that will determine whether the Cubs can truly contend for an NL Central title . The Cubs and Brewers square off seven times in that span, with Monday's victory putting the North Siders 7 games back of first-place Milwaukee. Despite their record-setting long balls, the Cubs finished August with a 16-12 record and were unable to put much pressure on the Brewers.

"We get 13 chances to play the Brewers, and then other than that, we don't have any control of the Brewers. They've got to go play their games, and we go play our games," Counsell said before the Cubs' big win. "They're on pace for a big number, I think they're on over a 100-win pace, that's hard to keep up with. You can go ask the rest of Major League Baseball, that's just hard to keep up with. They're having a fabulous season.

"They're a good team. I'm not surprised by that, not surprised at all. We're a good team. I mean, we're not going to be a 100-win team this year. We're a good team. So, that's the story right now."

The Cubs have seen their once sizeable hold on the NL's top wild-card spot evaporate over the last 10 days between a tough West Coast trip and dropping their weekend series against the Cincinnati Reds. The surging Phillies moved into a tie for the first NL wild-card position entering Monday, though the Cubs hold the season series tiebreaker over Philadelphia.

Counsell said the players aren't worrying about postseason positioning right now.

"Does everybody want to play at home as many games as we can? Absolutely, absolutely. We want to play at home. Are we going to shy away from a challenge on the road? Nope. So, that's how we look at it, and that's how every competitor looks at it."
