articles.title: Yankees' 5 Biggest Fears That Will Determine MLB Playoff Fate From Aaron Judge to George Lombard
articles.summary: After a long stay in a wilderness of mediocrity, things are looking up again for the New York Yankees.
articles.body:
After a long stay in a wilderness of mediocrity, things are looking up again for the New York Yankees.

They have won 10 out of 15, washing away with the sour taste of the 32-32 run that came before. They just clinched their season series with the Boston Red Sox. They can count the days until three-time MVP Aaron Judge is back.

As it is, the Yankees would be the American League's top wild-card team if the season ended today. Even better, FanDuel has them at +800 to win the World Series, the best of any team in the AL.

If anyone has been sensing a "But…" coming, here it is: The Yankees haven't actually won anything yet, and they still have much to worry about.

That first part is just objectively true. As for that second part, let's break down the Yankees' five biggest remaining fears in the form of questions.

In the blink of an eye, the question of whether Judge will return this season has switched from an "if" thing to a "when" thing. He's resumed baseball activities and is even with the team for a six-game road trip on the West Coast.

If Judge's time away with a rib injury has proved anything, it's that the 34-year-old's MVP credentials might actually undersell his value to his team:

Nonetheless, the question remains: How sure can anyone be that Judge will be Judge again?

He may well be the GOAT right-handed hitter , but is he so good that he can get back in the swing of things without the benefit of a rehab assignment? He wants to find out , but the Yankees might want to insist otherwise.

After all, even GOATs shouldn't be too confident after three months off. And in the case of this GOAT, Judge wasn't hot when he landed on the IL. He had batted .207 with just two home runs over his last 22 games.

Can Any of the Incumbents Pick Up Giancarlo Stanton's Torch?

Even if Judge returns and starts hitting like an MVP again, the Yankees can't take it for granted that he alone can carry a World Series pursuit.

This is partly a knock on Judge, whose career playoff OPS is 200 points below his career regular-season OPS. It's also just a recognition that even someone as awesome as Judge needs help every now and again.

This is where Giancarlo Stanton pulled through when the Yankees went to the World Series in 2024, going off for a 1.048 OPS and seven homers. He somehow usurped Judge and Juan Soto in the spotlight.

Why bring it up? In part because Stanton is likely done for the year after sustaining a new calf injury, but also because of how New York's hitters have performed since Judge went down on May 31. Only two of their top 10 most oft-used batters have posted an above-average wRC+ (i.e., over 100):

Thank goodness for Luis García Jr. , who has posted a 146 wRC+ since joining the Yankees ahead of the trade deadline. And sure, Jazz Chisholm Jr. (135 wRC+) has been warm if you only look as far back as August 4.

On the whole, though, the Yankees' Judge-less offense has been a rudderless ship. They probably don't want to find out what that could mean if nothing changes.

As a final point about the Yankees' everyday lineup, does anyone have a good take on who should be their shortstop come October?

The position has produced 2.7 rWAR this year, but 2.1 comes courtesy of glove-first utility infielder José Caballero . He was at short before Anthony Volpe failed his latest audition. Then the position passed to George Lombard Jr. , who had everyone feeling impressed before the wheels fell off.

Lombard started out hitting .320 through his first seven games, and then .222 in his next 16 games after that. He also committed an error in six straight games, and now he's day-to-day with knee discomfort .

Volpe is arguably worth another shot in response to the heater he's been at Triple-A, where he has a 1.036 OPS over 12 games. It's more likely that this is Lombard's job until the Yankees are convinced it shouldn't be.

Obviously, the rookie is not trending well in this regard. If he can't reverse course, the light-hitting Caballero might reclaim shortstop by default.

The Yankees were linked to all sorts of bullpen upgrades before the trade deadline, including heavyweights like Mason Miller and Adrian Morejon . Yet they ended up empty-handed.

So, how bad has it been since then? Well, the Yankees have a 2.87 bullpen ERA since August 4. Strange but true, and it's largely a credit to a back-end duo of David Bednar and Brent Headrick that has been solid all year.

At the same time, the Yankees have enjoyed unsustainably strong performances from guys like Paul Blackburn and Tim Hill . The bullpen has otherwise been a veritable carousel of fringe relievers in recent weeks, and it now faces the prospect of being without Fernando Cruz for the rest of the year .

It isn't the best status quo for a bullpen that has been undermanned all year. With the trade deadline in the past, hope of stability now rests on converted starters like Luis Gil and ( eventually ) Clarke Schmidt .

It could work. Or, it could be a disaster that proves the Yankees should have been more aggressive pursuing trades when they had the chance.

It's not some big secret what makes this Yankees team dangerous. It's starting pitching.

Yankees starters lead MLB with a 3.36 ERA, and the guys who need to be healthy are healthy. Cam Schlittler , Gerrit Cole , Max Fried and Carlos Rodón are all right where they belong.

However, Cole, Fried and Rodón have spent time on the IL this year with arm-related ailments. Schlittler hasn't, yet the fear with him is connected to how he's already blown past his previous career high for innings:

This is with a month still to go before October, and there are already points of concern at play with the hard-throwing righty. Relative to the first half, Schlittler is walking more batters and allowing more hard contact thus far in the second half.

Schlittler is the front-runner for the AL Cy Young Award, so it goes without saying that he's the favorite to be New York's Game 1 starter in the playoffs. The last thing they need is him crumbling under the weight of fatigue.

The question lingering in the background is simple: If not the Yankees as AL favorites, then who?

Yeah, you've got me there. Their 78-60 record may be 4.5 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays for the best in the AL, but the Yankees' +108 run differential is easily the best. Because of the Judge factor, they also have the most potential left to tap into of any contender in the AL.

Given these circumstances, though, there should be a stronger feeling that this is the Yankees' year than there actually is. Doubt persists, and it persists precisely because of the fears laid out above.

Until they turn those questions into old news, the Yankees will remain in "prove it" territory.

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

articles.title: MLB's Biggest Breakouts of 2026, Ranked
articles.summary: The best stories in sports are usually the ones that no one saw coming, such as Major League Baseball's biggest breakout players of the 2026 campaign.
articles.body:
The best stories in sports are usually the ones that no one saw coming, such as Major League Baseball's biggest breakout players of the 2026 campaign.

Before we dive in, a few points of clarification on what does and does not qualify as a breakout:

"Bounce-Back Players" and "Breakout Players" are two completely separate things. For instance, Yordan Alvarez had a brutal 2025 campaign and Eduardo Rodríguez was barely a replacement-level pitcher over the past two seasons. They've been fantastic this year, but they had previously established themselves as quality players with roughly 20 WAR apiece heading into this season. Neither will appear on this ranking.

Rookie of the Year candidates who were already top prospects coming into this season also do not qualify as breakouts. Kevin McGonigle, JJ Wetherholt and Nolan McLean were consensus top 10 prospects in the preseason. Carson Benge, Payton Tolle, Sal Stewart and Chase DeLauter weren't terribly far behind them. And both Munetaka Murakami and Kazuma Okamoto were paid handsomely to come over from Japan. They didn't break out. They arrived.

However, we are including rookies like Tristan Peters and Foster Griffin who have played major roles out of seemingly nowhere. So, it's not a blanket "no rookies" rule, but more of a "no rookies who we expected to be good" rule.

Without further ado, we give you this season's top 25 breakout players.

Unfortunately, we open this list with back-to-back-to-back breakout players who are currently broken. Brown has been out since late June with a neck injury, but he was Chicago's most valuable pitcher when he hit the shelf, logging 68.0 innings with a 1.85 ERA as their swing man—after posting a 5.92 ERA in the same role last year.

24. Justin Wrobleski, LHP, Los Angeles Dodgers

Wrobleski landed on the IL a couple weeks ago with a forearm strain, but what would the Dodgers have done without this surprise All-Star while Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow and Shohei Ohtani weren't pitching? He had a 4.81 ERA over the past two seasons as an occasional starter/bulk reliever, but he has logged the second-most innings pitched among Dodgers this season with a 3.56 ERA.

23. Curtis Mead, 3B, Boston Red Sox / Washington Nationals

Mead was a top prospect once upon a time, but it took several years for him to look the part. He broke out in a huge way for the Nationals this year, with 17 home runs and an .852 OPS in 88 games played. Comparatively, he had five home runs and a .617 OPS in 152 games played over the previous three seasons. It's really too bad, though, that he suffered a fractured wrist in his second plate appearance after Boston traded for him.

22. Paul Blackburn, RHP and Brent Headrick, LHP, New York Yankees

Over the previous nine seasons, Blackburn had a 4.97 ERA, mostly as a starting pitcher. And in a three-season career that encompassed just 32 appearances, Headrick had a 4.70 ERA. So, color us surprised that they have mutually morphed into one of the best one-two punches in baseball's middle relief corps, each with a sub-2.00 ERA for the year. In fact, Blackburn has a 0.61 ERA across his last 32 appearances and is probably going to be New York's primary eighth-inning arm in the postseason.

Melton flashed some real potential over the final 10 weeks of last season, making 16 appearances (four starts) with a 2.76 ERA. He even made four appearances in the postseason. It's still a surprise, though, that he has blossomed into arguably the ace of this staff with a 1.86 ERA in 16 starts. If he hadn't missed the first two months, he might be in the mix for AL Cy Young—and maybe the Tigers wouldn't have struggled as badly as they did early on.

Baker had a respectable four-year run with the Orioles from 2022-25, making 173 appearances with a 3.73 ERA. He even saved a few games for the O's. Still, who could have guessed in the preseason that Baker would be MLB's leader in saves, with 39 of them to go along with his 1.50 ERA? He is the first of three surprisingly dominant closers on this list.

Rumfield is probably going to finish fourth or fifth in the NL Rookie of the Year vote, but he very much was not on the tier of a Kevin McGonigle or JJ Wetherholt as far as preseason rookie-year expectations went. In fact, Steamer had him projected for 78 games played and a minus-0.1 WAR. Yet, he might mess around and lead the NL in on-base percentage, presently triple-slashing .289/.380/.437, cementing himself as Colorado's everyday first baseman.

18. Liam Hicks, C, Tampa Bay Rays / Miami Marlins

In nearly 1,100 plate appearances in the minors from 2021-24, Hicks hit a grand total of 13 home runs. He also had a mediocre .693 OPS while playing in 119 games for the Marlins last season. But he blew up this year with 14 home runs in 409 trips to the plate with Miami, before getting traded to Tampa Bay and putting together a .945 OPS since the deadline.

Surprise closer No. 2 on the list, Latz's first appearance of the season was actually as a starter. With Jacob deGrom a late scratch due to a stiff neck, Latz went four hitless innings against the Phillies on March 28. About a month later, he recorded the second save of his career and has yet to look back. The 2026 All-Star has gone 27-for-29 on save chances since stepping into the role, and has a 1.65 ERA for the year.

Meyer was the No. 3 overall pick in 2020 and a staple in "preseason top 100 prospects" rankings over the course of the subsequent four springs. But injuries limited his innings and his production, entering 2026 with a 5.29 ERA in 25 career starts in the majors. Though injuries have unfortunately derailed things for Meyer once again, he had a 2.68 ERA in 20 starts and was named an All-Star before landing back on the IL again.

Save for one Cy Young favorite flamethrower in the top five, Lopez has the highest bWAR (5.4) among players on this list, ranking top 10 among all position players. He previously had been a quality defender, but he has significantly upped his game at the plate. Lopez's OPS is more than 100 points higher than it had been between 2024-25, and he's likely to finish top 10 in the majors in both batting average (.305) and stolen bases (29).

14. Foster Griffin, LHP, Cleveland Guardians / Washington Nationals

Griffin was a first-round pick in 2014, but he logged just 8.0 innings pitched in the majors over the next eight seasons before taking his talents to Japan. In three years with the Yomiuri Giants, he had a 2.57 ERA, convincing the Nationals to take a flyer on bringing him back to the States. He became arguably the ace of the staff, making 22 starts with a 3.06 ERA and earning a spot on the All-Star roster before getting traded to Cleveland.

13. Louis Varland, RHP, Toronto Blue Jays

In Baker, Latz and Varland, what a year it has been for breakout closers in the American League. Prior to this season, Varland had never saved a game in the majors or the minors, and he only got the job because Jeff Hoffman couldn't save anything through the first three weeks. He has been nearly perfect, though, going 31-for-32 in save chances with a minuscule 1.12 ERA.

12. Jac Caglianone, RF, Kansas City Royals

It's tough to say where Cags should slot on this list. He was a disaster in the majors last season, his .157 batting average good for dead last among players who made at least 200 plate appearances. However, he was the No. 6 overall pick in 2024, subsequently smashing his way through the minors. So, even though he has broken through in a huge way with 23 home runs and an .832 OPS, it isn't terribly surprising.

See: Caglianone, Jac. Got to have him somewhere on this list, but it'd feel weird to call it a top-10 breakout story. Burns went No. 2 overall in 2024, mowing through the minors and making his MLB debut less than 12 months later. He had a 5.24 ERA through his first eight starts before missing five weeks with an elbow injury and returning as a reliever for the home stretch. But like Caglianone, we expected big things for his sophomore season. He has delivered in a huge way, likely to finish top five in the NL Cy Young vote.

Burke was Chicago's Opening Day starter in 2025, and he did go six scoreless innings in that game. It was otherwise an uninspiring season, though, giving up six earned runs in his next outing and never again getting his ERA back below 4.00. Fast-forward to 2026 and he has had one of the most valuable four-seam fastballs in the business and a K/BB ratio 50 percent better than last year. He has been Chicago's most valuable pitcher throughout this improbable turnaround.

9. Kyle Harrison, LHP, Milwaukee Brewers

In three seasons with the Giants, Harrison was just OK. An occasional gem here and there, but a 4.48 ERA and 8.8 K/9 overall as a marginally better-than-replacement-level pitcher. The Brewers have managed to unlock his potential, though, boasting a 2.79 ERA and 11.1 K/9 through 21 starts. He doesn't often pitch deep into games, but he has given them at least five solid innings in two out of every three times he takes the mound.

8. Cade Cavalli, RHP, Washington Nationals

Cavalli's path to this breakout season was marred by injury. He made one appearance in the big leagues in 2022 before disappearing for nearly three years, injuring his shoulder in that game and undergoing Tommy John surgery the following spring. He finally made it back for 10 starts last season with a 4.25 ERA, striking out 18.3 percent of batters faced. But now he's a star on the rise with marks of 3.12 ERA and 27.7 percent strikeout rate.

Over the previous two seasons, Durán played in 182 games for the Rangers, appearing at least once at every position except for catcher. But he did so with a .587 OPS, three home runs and a glove that was versatile, but unremarkable. He was both a replacement player and a replacement-level player. This year, however, he has a .780 OPS, 15 home runs and an extremely strong case to win the American League's Utility Gold Glove.

Like Foster Griffin, Lambert was pitching in Japan a year ago. But at least Griffin was doing it well. Lambert—who had a 6.28 ERA in four seasons with the Rockies—barely maintained a 4.00 ERA overseas and had to take a minor league deal to get another shot at the majors. As the Astros were riddled with pitching injuries early in the year, though, Lambert made the most of his opportunity with a 3.11 ERA across his first 21 starts, pitching at least into the fifth inning of each one.

5. Jacob Misiorowski, RHP, Milwaukee Brewers

You might be wondering: How can a guy who was already an All-Star last year be one of the top five breakouts of this season?

Well, 2025 Jacob Misiorowski was more of a viral sensation than a superstar. He was a sideshow as opposed to the main event.

He threw his four-seamer approximately one million miles per hour. However, he walked too many batters (4.2 BB/9) and his breaking balls were a little too hittable. The fact that he threw his slider in the mid-90s was mind-blowing, but opponents hit nearly .300 against it, resulting in a 4.36 ERA and a bWAR of just 0.5 .

He also simply wasn't very durable, pitching more than five innings in just three of his 15 appearances.

This year, though, The Miz has become not just a bona fide ace—with 17 quality starts and three or fewer earned runs allowed in each of his 25 outings—but one of the most dominant forces on the mound in recent memory.

His walk rate (2.1 BB/9) is half of what it was as a rookie, and both his slider and curveball have gone from "mediocre pitches" to "devastating offerings." He's leading the majors in both ERA (1.73) and strikeouts (222). He is two wins (14) behind the MLB leaders in that third and final Triple Crown category.

He received zero Cy Young votes and just two vote points for NL ROY last year. But barring a September collapse, he's probably going to win the Cy Young unanimously and certainly should finish top-five in the NL MVP vote.

It's hard to believe this is the same Miguel Vargas that the White Sox acquired from the Dodgers at the 2024 trade deadline.

After a woeful final two months of that campaign, he entered 2025 as a career .175/.273/.312 hitter. On just about any other team, he would have been out of a job. But with the rebuilding White Sox, he remained Plan A at the hot corner and started to turn things around last year.

It wasn't until this season, though, that he really broke out.

Vargas is leading the American League with 92 runs scored. He also has 29 home runs, 76 RBI and 13 stolen bases, all of which are already career highs by a wide margin.

In addition to those sky-rocketing counting stats, his bat speed has increased substantially.

He was well below the league average at 70.6 mph last season , and even slower in 2024 at 69.8 mph. But he is up to 73.9 mph this year, resulting in harder-hit balls and one of the highest expected slugging percentages (.519) in the majors.

On top of that, not only did Vargas make the roster for the All-Star Game, but he was also the only player to homer in that game. That's how you punctuate a breakout year.

3. Jake Bauers, 1B/OF, Milwaukee Brewers

For as drastically as Jacob Misiorowski has improved since last season, he isn't even the biggest breakout among Brewers named Jacob/Jakob.

Through Jake Bauers' first six seasons in the big leagues, he was worth a cumulative minus-1.2 bWAR .

The 2025 season ended up being his best of those years, but even that wasn't going to be the case until he caught fire down the stretch with a 1.072 OPS from Sept. 5 onward. Prior to that, he was once again a sub-replacement-level player, despite the fact that Milwaukee almost exclusively deployed his left-handed bat against right-handed pitching.

This year has been a completely different story.

If there were MVP awards for spring training, Bauers might have won it, batting .462/.571/1.154 with seven home runs. And then with both Jackson Chourio and Andrew Vaughn missing all of April on the IL, Bauers was given every opportunity to prove he could be more than just a platoon guy.

He rose to the challenge and then some, becoming Milwaukee's best hitter with 23 home runs and an .885 OPS. Rather than avoiding southpaws, he has owned them, slugging .541 in 132 plate appearances against lefties—up from a .333 mark in his career prior to 2026.

2. Jordan Walker, OF, St. Louis Cardinals

We just noted Jake Bauers entered this season with a minus-1.2 career bWAR before finally breaking through.

Well, Jordan Walker was at a minus-2.6 bWAR for his career after a downright horrific 2025 campaign. In fact, his minus-1.7 mark for last season put him in a tie with LaMonte Wade Jr. for worst among all position players .

But Walker arrived in 2023 with so much promise, a consensus top five prospect in all of baseball after he roped through Double-A in 2022 with a .306 batting average, 19 home runs and 22 stolen bases.

That potential superstar was nowhere to be found in 2024 or 2025, though. Walker had a .595 OPS in 162 games played.

Instead of hitting like the next Aaron Judge, he was hitting like the next Ke'Bryan Hayes, but without the elite glovework.

So, he went back to the drawing board and completely changed his stance at the dish.

Per Statcast , Walker's stance angle in 2023 and 2024 was more than 40 degrees open. Not exactly old school Tony Batista staring the pitcher square in the face, but it was the sixth-most open stance in the majors during those two seasons.

Not that there's anything inherently wrong with that. Rafael Devers has the widest-open stance in baseball these days, and he's one heck of a hitter.

It wasn't working for Walker, though, so now he's down to one degree open and has been raking to the tune of an .839 OPS and 27 home runs.

He also has 18 stolen bases and is probably going to get to 30 HR and 20 SB before we reach the finish line. If he does, he'll be the first Cardinal to do so since Fernando Tatis Sr. in 1999.

1. Tristan Peters, OF, Chicago White Sox

Not only has Tristan Peters been an incredible breakout story, but "Bananas Bonds" is also an all-timer of a baseball nickname.

The Bananas part is, of course, an homage to his time with the Savannah Bananas during the summer of 2021—before they became the barnstorming exhibition-game sensation they are today.

But the Bonds part is a testament to the overnight celebrity of slugging that he has become.

Peters was originally drafted by the Brewers in the seventh round in 2021. He was later traded to the Giants for Trevor Rosenthal; San Francisco subsequently traded him to the Rays for Brett Wisely. (Curiously enough, Wisely is also a Savannah Bananas alum.)

After three years in the Rays' farm system, he appeared in four big league games last summer, going 0-for-12 with seven strikeouts. They designated him for assignment in December and ended up trading him to the White Sox for future considerations.

To put it gently, Peters wasn't the preseason favorite for AL Rookie of the Year.

He narrowly made the cut for the Opening Day roster, and perhaps only because Brooks Baldwin suffered what turned out to be a season-ending elbow injury during spring training. But Peters quickly became a regular in the lineup, albeit with a .629 OPS and no home runs through the team's first 45 games.

Since May 17, though, he has triple-slashed .289/.355/.526 with a dozen home runs.

He hit for the cycle on July 10. He recently homered in five consecutive games. And if he plays a key role in getting the White Sox to the World Series, we'll go Bananas.

articles.title: September sports watch guide: NFL kickoff, Kiffin vs. Ole Miss, WNBA and MLB playoffs
articles.summary: “Summer has come and passed.” That’s a bummer for just about everyone, save for pumpkin spice lobbyists and Richard Gere. Fear not, though — we’re about to h...
articles.body:
" Summer has come and passed ." That's a bummer for just about everyone, save for pumpkin spice lobbyists and Richard Gere . Fear not, though — we're about to hit the coolest stretch of the sports calendar.

September is full of worthwhile watches. NFL and college football officially kick off. Men's and women's soccer leagues ramp up. MLB and the WNBA reach their respective playoffs. There's U.S. Open tennis and Presidents Cup golf; the chill of an NHL puck drop and the heat of the Spanish Grand Prix. "Chad Powers" is back under center, lest we forget.

This is The Athletic 's comprehensive guide to sports in September. For the sake of time and space, we weren't able to cover everything for the month to come. But we did our best to properly celebrate such a vast slate. All times are ET, and all channel listings are for U.S. viewers.

You can watch live sports on Fubo ( Stream Free Now ).

This latest installment of the "Untold" documentary series centers on Rachael Gunn, the Australian breakdancer who competed in her newly recognized Olympic sport. Memes and misnomers ensued.

Women's volleyball Big Ten/SEC Challenge

Sept. 1-6 on B1G+, Big Ten Network, ESPN2, Fox, FS1, SECN+, SEC Network

All 18 Big Ten and 16 SEC programs are in this inaugural interconference clash. The finale is a Fox doubleheader at Wrigley Field , with Kentucky facing Penn State and Nebraska playing Missouri.

Glen Powell is the titular catfish quarterback of the South Georgia Catfish. Eli Manning, producer and founder of the original bit , had a cameo in the first season. All six episodes drop simultaneously.

'On Campus: Game of the Week' series premiere

It's Netflix's spin on the "College GameDay" concept, with two students leading the camera across campus sites and tailgate shenanigans each week. Thankfully, there's no Pat McAfee in this one.

The season starts with the London City Lionesses hosting Manchester United. The league has expanded to 14 clubs after the promotion of Birmingham City, Charlton Athletic and Crystal Palace. Three-time WSL Golden Boot winner Khadija Shaw suits up for defending champion Manchester City, which welcomes Birmingham on Sept. 6.

The 20th FIBA Women's World Cup is commemorated in Berlin. Team USA is stacked with stars like Paige Bueckers, Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese. The U.S. is going for a fifth straight championship; it starts group play with China, Czechia and Italy.

Wisconsin vs. Notre Dame (Shamrock Series)

Heisman Trophy hype machine CJ Carr leads the No. 4 Fighting Irish into historic Lambeau Field. The Badgers counter with fleet quarterback Colton Joseph, who transferred from Old Dominion. Wisconsin fans have the in-state advantage here, but Notre Dame always travels well.

This MLS and Liga MX crossover comes down to four Mexican clubs. The winners of Toluca versus León and América versus Monterrey play for the title. Each of the top three finishers qualify for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup, and the victor goes straight into the round of 16.

Men's Champions League: League Phase Matchday 1

As always, the UCL field is loaded to the brim. French titan Paris Saint-Germain bids for a three-peat with Ousmane Dembélé. Declan Rice and EPL champion Arsenal embark on a redemption tour . Bundesliga club Bayern Munich has Harry Kane , and La Liga's Barcelona has Lamine Yamal. Soccer's great gauntlet never disappoints.

New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks

The NFL kicks off its new season with a rematch of last season's Super Bowl. Drake Maye and the Pats visit Sam Darnold and the 12s on "Sunday Night Football," which is on a Wednesday this time. Sure. New England arrives after the A.J. Brown trade and the Mike Vrabel saga ; Seattle raises a second banner as team ownership changes over.

All four WPBL teams — the Boston Hunters, Los Angeles Queens, New York Heights and San Francisco Firebells — make the first postseason. It's a best-of-three semifinals and a best-of-five championship series. Among the notable names are No. 1 pick Kelsie Whitmore and former Little League standout Mo'ne Davis.

San Francisco 49ers vs. Los Angeles Rams

Division rivals and Super Bowl aspirants begin their 2026 campaigns at Melbourne Cricket Ground. This Netflix exclusive marks the NFL's regular-season debut in Australia. New Rams pass rusher Myles Garrett pairs with the unretired Aaron Donald , while Niners running back Christian McCaffrey adds star wattage on the other sideline. Head coaches Sean McVay and Kyle Shanahan are two of the league's top play callers .

Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands hosts this women's tourney between the U.S. and Europe. Angela Stanford captains the American side, while Swedish mainstay Anna Nordqvist leads the Europeans. The first two days are foursomes and four-ball matches; the third day shifts to singles.

Tennis takes Queens, N.Y., for the last Grand Slam of the season. Defending men's champion Carlos Alcaraz returns from a wrist injury and now seeks his fourth major championship in two years. On the women's side, Aryna Sabalenka tries to conquer the tournament for a third consecutive time. The women's final on Sept. 12 starts at 4 p.m. on ESPN, while the men's final is the following day at 2 p.m. on ABC.

We've got a top-five powerhouse headliner, with "College GameDay" on campus in Austin. Quarterbacks Julian Sayin and Arch Manning are Heisman hopefuls. Wideouts Jeremiah Smith and Cam Coleman look like NFL Draft gems. This has game-of-the-year potential .

Sept. 12, 8 p.m. on Paramount+ (main card)

A long lineage of Las Vegas boxing spectacles continues with Garcia, who holds the WBC welterweight title, and Benn, his mandatory challenger. Benn's father, Nigel, won the belt as a super middleweight in 1992.

Madring's maiden F1 race offers the longest banked turn on the circuit. McLaren teammates Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris finished first and second in last year's run, which was held in Barcelona.

Sept. 13, 11:30 a.m. on NBC, NBCSN/Peacock or USA

City's Erling Haaland and United's Bruno Fernandes stand atop The Athletic 's Premier League rankings . Old Trafford is the " Theatre of Dreams ." The derby paints heroes and villains in reds and blues, with enough natural pageantry to demand a worldwide audience.

A new kind of booing might be invented at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Lane Kiffin guided Ole Miss to its most promising year in several lifetimes, then left to coach fellow SEC member LSU without any love lost . Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels certainly want to show out against Kiffin's remade Tigers. It's another "College GameDay" special as well.

The chase is on. Denny Hamlin enters the 10-race playoff atop the points table, with a No. 1 seed to boost his odds at a first career NASCAR Cup Series title. Others in the field of 16 include No. 2 Ryan Blaney, No. 3 Tyler Reddick and No. 4 Ty Gibbs. The playoffs run through Nov. 8, but few tracks can match the pull of Bristol Motor Speedway.

Kevin Hart's 'Cold as Balls' Season 13 premiere

Fresh episodes of the ice bath interview show feature Novak Djokovic, Cooper Flagg, Rob Gronkowski, Zlatan Ibrahimović and Serena Williams. Yes, Hart is shorter than all of his guests.

Women's Champions League: League Phase Matchday 1

Barcelona has been a force, winning three of the last four UEFA titles. It still has midfielder Aitana Bonmatí, a three-time Ballon d'Or recipient. But pressure builds from the likes of OL Lyonnes, which adds forward Salma Paralluelo from Barca, and 2025 champion Arsenal.

At his peak, Jackson was one of the NFL's most magnetic talents, a vertical game-breaker with swagger to spare. This documentary uses footage from his brother, Byron, tracing the receiver's journey from Pop Warner to the pros.

Sept. 24-27 on Golf Channel, NBC and Peacock

Led by world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler and team captain Brandt Snedeker, the U.S. tries to get back on top of intercontinental golf and avenge its 2025 Ryder Cup loss. The Americans have claimed 10 straight Presidents Cups since a tie in 2003. The international team (sans Europe) stars South Korean Si Woo Kim and is captained by Australian Geoff Ogilvy. All four days are at Chicago's Medinah Country Club.

The NFL's international schedule is bigger than ever this year, with nine matchups spread across seven different countries. This one brings the Ravens and Cowboys to Rio de Janeiro. Points should come wholesale between Baltimore's ground game (Lamar Jackson, Derrick Henry) and Dallas' air attack (Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb).

Sept. 27 on Disney networks (ABC, ESPN), Prime Video and USA

The bracket teems with hype and hope. A'ja Wilson and the Las Vegas Aces are the incumbent champs. Olivia Miles leads the Minnesota Lynx in pursuit of the franchise's fifth title. There are also the 3-and-D Golden State Valkyries, the star-laden New York Liberty, Caitlin Clark's Indiana Fever and Paige Bueckers' Dallas Wings. The playoffs run into October.

From South Central to Beverly Hills, "All American" dramatizes the culture clashes of Los Angeles high school football. The show, based on the life of former NFL linebacker and Super Bowl champ Spencer Paysinger, is wrapping up its eight-season arc.

Hockey is back, and it bumps up to an 84-game regular-season schedule. ESPN gets things going with a national TV three-piece. First, the Carolina Hurricanes raise their championship banner before hosting the Florida Panthers. Later on, the New York Rangers take the ice against the rival Boston Bruins, followed by the Chicago Blackhawks at the Vegas Golden Knights.

Playoff baseball brings on a distinct, rarified tension. The air thins and the game slows. Though there's still much to settle in the standings, 2026 wild cards could go to tentpoles like the Boston Red Sox, New York Yankees, Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia Phillies. All four best-of-three series are on NBC Sports.

From there, we shuffle into October — where the World Series and the almighty sports equinox await us.

articles.title: Yankees prospects: Week 23 minor league recap
articles.summary: Not much time left. Time for the playoff sprint.
articles.body:
There's not much time left in the minor league calendar, and the playoff races are heating up. While one affiliate has already punched their ticket, the other three are still searching for late runs to power their way there.

T riple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders

Record: 31-23 (68-60), 2.5 GB in the International League East after a 3-3 week against the Worcester Red Sox (Red Sox)

Coming up: Home vs. Lehigh Valley IronPigs (Phillies)

The RailRiders wrapped up a rough month of August with a contentious split, keeping them within an arm's length of a playoff spot with three weeks to go. They got a bit of a rough deal with Worcester hosting three different rehab assignments this week, including Roman Anthony, but fared pretty well until a rough day on Sunday.

The offense has a lot of name-brand talent already, but they decided to add another former top prospect to their ranks with a mid-week signing of Jarred Kelenic for the playoff push, because why not? Additionally, Mitch Garver is currently in roster limbo after exercising an assignment clause, but the fact he hasn't been added to the active roster by now likely closes the door on him getting recalled without an injury. Anthony Volpe (now getting reps at third base) and Marco Luciano carried the offense this week, combining for seven home runs on 18 hits.

The two prospects who've been here all season did not get to pitch here this week due to promotions to the big leagues, as Elmer Rodríguez is making a pair of spot starts until the schedule evens out while Brendan Beck was needed as the 27th man on Saturday. Alexander Cornielle won International League Pitcher of the Week with eight terrific shutout innings in the best start of his pro career, but the headline on the farm was the return of Kyle Carr, who got double duty on Tuesday and Sunday. He combined to allow three runs in three innings with Xavier Rivas as the piggyback. Let's just say it's not going well for the Ole Miss alum since his promotion.

The team needed two bullpen games due to the promotions, which we saw with Hayden Merda starting both games and tossing three solid innings combined. Eric Reyzelman and Eli Morgan both had terrific weeks as well, and with the rapidly thinning bullpen depth becoming an issue (one attempt to be resolved by claiming John Schreiber on waivers), both could be on the major league radar for cameos down the stretch.

Jasson Domínguez: .269/.347/.420, 7 HR, 29 RBI, 11 SB, 101 wRC+ Anthony Volpe: .235/.313/.504, 8 HR, 20 RBI, 15 XBH, 106 wRC+ (134 PA) Oswaldo Cabrera: .286/.343/.443, 17 HR, 59 RBI, 31 XBH, 103 wRC+ Brendan Beck: 9-2, 2.75 ERA, 3.35 FIP, 1.05 WHIP, 19.9 K-BB% (121 IP) Elmer Rodríguez: 8-3, 2.59 ERA, 3.72 FIP, 1.26 WHIP, 13.1 K-BB% (97.1 IP)

Record: 30-27 (67-59), 3.5 GB in the Eastern League Northeast after a 3-3 week against the Akron RubberDucks (Guardians)

Coming up: Away @ Erie SeaWolves (Tigers)

Somerset had a perfectly fine week, trading wins and losses without anything too good or bad happening. The problem was, in a heated playoff race, splitting sometimes isn't good enough. They lost 2.5 games of ground this week, with scorching hot Reading going up 3.5 games. With 12 to go, these guys are going to have to play some of their best baseball.

It was a fairly pedestrian week for the offense. Jace Avina has had a really crummy month (.213/.314/.258) and will look to turn the page next week, while Roderick Arias and Josh Moylan continue to excel after summer promotions. I want to highlight Manuel Palencia here, who's been one of the best hitters in the system for two months now. After entering July with an abhorrent .504 OPS, he's slashed .351/.380/.596 with a 157 wRC+ in 121 plate appearances over the last two months. His stock is finally gaining some helium.

For the bruised and battered rotation, we saw a struggle of a start from Cade Smith (5.2 IP, 5 R), a 10-strikeout quality start from Dom Hamel, and a rehab appearance by Clarke Schmidt. The two big storylines were two guys who weren't here last week. Bryce Cunningham made his Double-A debut on Tuesday and played double duty on Sunday, combining to allow nine runs in 11 innings with 13 strikeouts. We also saw the return of the struggling Chase Hampton, who missed three weeks on the temporarily inactive list. He tossed four solid innings with six strikeouts, hopefully a sign of things to come.

It was an uneven week for the bullpen, which technically counts Rory Fox's piggyback effort behind Schmidt, where he tossed 5.1 solid innings. Trent Sellers, Michael Arias, Kevin Stevens, and Geoff Gilbert all excelled this week, while others struggled to put up zeroes.

Jace Avina: .250/.347/.466, 19 HR, 62 RBI, 48 XBH, 23.6 K%, 119 wRC+ DJ Gladney: .268/.331/.509, 23 HR, 85 RBI, 19 SB, 121 wRC+ Coby Morales: .280/.372/.486, 20 HR, 77 RBI, 44 XBH, 131 wRC+ Cade Smith: 7-8, 4.98 ERA, 5.43 FIP, 1.44 WHIP, 12.5 K-BB% (110.1 IP) Ben Hess: 3-4, 4.45 ERA, 4,69 FIP, 1.45 WHIP, 13.7 K-BB% (56.2 IP , injured)

Record: 34-26 (64-60), 3 GB in the South Atlantic League North after a 3-3 week against the Brooklyn Cyclones (Mets)

Coming up: Away @ Wilmington Blue Rocks (Nationals)

Hudson Valley extended their win streak to nine games on Tuesday, but struggled the rest of the week as their momentum fizzled out and their playoff hopes dwindled with it. Suddenly, they're going to need to make up three games this week against Wilmington to get in. The division-leading Frederick Keys won the first half, which would invoke other tiebreakers, but the Renegades would lose out on a playoff spot in that scenario to Greensboro, so they'll need to jump two teams here.

The split wasn't because of any offensive ineptitude. David McCann homered twice, Jackson Lovich had four extra-base hits, Kyle West had three, and Hans Montero went 6-for-10 across three games. With only a week left in the regular season, you're looking for guys to finish strong, and that's certainly what Lovich is doing. After striking out nearly 40 percent of the time in his first few weeks at the level, he's put up a 10-game stretch where he's limited them while walking at a significantly higher rate. He was an early-season darling, but is putting together a good body of work in his first full season in the pros.

The bullpen was really ugly this week, so they get most of the blame instead of the starters, who actually pitched quite well. Allen Facundo tossed a quality start (6 IP, 2 R), Luis Serna struck out seven in 4.2 shutout innings, Sean Paul Liñan allowed three runs in five innings, and both Danny Flatt and Brandon Decker pitched brief, scoreless outings in emergency roles. The former had been sent down to the FCL two weeks ago, so that was his High-A debut.

Eric Genther: .273/.407/.441, 12 HR, 57 RBI, 31 XBH, 128 wRC+ David McCann (FCL/A/A+): .284/.374/.572, 16 HR, 54 RBI, 26 XBH, 136 wRC+ Jackson Lovich (A/A+): .287/.363/.506, 22 HR, 84 RBI, 36 SB, 28.6 K%, 123 wRC+ Luis Serna: 6-5, 3.98 ERA, 3.59 FIP, 1.15 WHIP, 20.5 K-BB% (108.2 IP) Allen Facundo: 5-3, 4.64 ERA, 4.43 FIP, 1.44 WHIP, 11.6 K-BB% (94.1 IP)

Record: 39-18 (71-46), 9 GA in the Florida State League West after a 5-0 week against the Jupiter Hammerheads (Marlins)

Coming up: Home vs. Dunedin Blue Jays (Blue Jays)

These guys just keep raking. They outscored a good Jupiter team 41 to 15 in a five-game sweep, marking a 10th consecutive series without a defeat. They're 8-0-2 in series since mid-June and clinched the Florida State League West Division with nine games to spare. It's been a truly special few months for the Tarpons.

The offense is still really good. We're going back to the running tally:

Yostin Pena continues to be a wrecking ball. He went 5-for-13 with a monster home run on Sunday, while also drawing six walks. That last part is important, as he had entred this week with a grand total of one walk in several weeks in Single-A.

Dax Kilby went 4-for-18 with a home run, double, and seven walks. No guy is more content to take ball four than Kilby, who also hit a new max exit velocity at 108.9.

Paul Gutierrez-Contreras II went 6-for-13 with a home run.

Bear Harrison, who was off to a horrible start to his pro career, went 4-for-12 with two doubles and five RBIs. Good week for him.

Tyce Armstrong went 8-for-16 with three homers and two doubles, winning FSL Player of the Week. This is a guy who hit nukes at Baylor and should rise quickly.

The rotation didn't need to be spectacular this week, but they were pretty good. Wyatt Parliament seems to be getting load-managed down the stretch, only tossing 3.1 scoreless innings. Edinzo Marquez and Tyler Boudreau both tossed five one-run innings, but the latter was awarded a complete game due to rain shortening his start. Sabier Marte struck out nine but gave up five runs in his start, but the crown jewel of the week was J.T. Etheridge's best start of his pro career, striking out 10 in six magnificent innings.

Pretty much everyone in the bullpen looked sharp, with the exception of Antonio Gomez's second outing of the week. His stuff is still nasty, but he's a work in progress. The guy of note here is Matthew Tippie, who throws a forkball and has been brilliant for a few months now. Since May 14, he's pitched to a 0.86 ERA with a 20.9 K-BB% in 31.1 innings. There's also Justin West, who struck out nine in a piggyback start and continues to be electric over the last two months.

Luis Escudero: .281/.460/.540, 10 HR, 28 RBI, 17 SB, 160 wRC+ Yostin Pena (DSL/A): .368/.444/.632, 13 HR, 79 RBI, 34 SB, 154 wRC+ Dax Kilby: .272/.444/.437, 3 HR, 23 RBI, 11 SB, 142 wRC+ (135 PA) Tyler Boudreau: 7-3, 3.51 ERA, 4.04 FIP, 1.06 WHIP, 17.1 K-BB% (100 IP) Justin West : 10-3, 4.08 ERA, 3.82 FIP, 1.24 WHIP, 19.1 K-BB% (108 IP)

DSL Yankees: Record: 33-21, 2 GB in DSL East. Eliminated in DSL Cup Pool Play Run differential: +141

DSL Bombers: Record: 25-29, 11 GB in DSL Southeast. Missed playoffs Run differential: +8

Isaias Castillo: .294/.408/.629, 14 HR, 49 RBI, 35 XBH, 28 SB, 132 wRC+ Juan Torres: .385/.470/.644, 8 HR, 65 RBI, 36 XBH, 26 SB, 159 wRC+ David Carrera: .333/.502/.594, 9 HR, 41 RBI, 23 XBH, 160 wRC+ Fredy Penuelas: 52 IP, 1.56 ERA, 3.91 FIP, 1.00 WHIP, 18.4 K-BB% Cesar Acosta : 51.2 IP, 3.31 ERA, 3.35 FIP, 1.01 WHIP, 24.1 K-BB%

Weekly Stats: 8-for-16, 3 HR, 9 RBI, 2 2B, 2 BB, 5 K, 1 SB Season Stats: .328/.427/.656, 5 HR, 22 RBI, 10 XBH, 16.0 BB%, 25.3 K%, 170 wRC+ (75 PA)

articles.title: Shane Bieber’s wife Kara Maxine Bieber’s pregnancy-era style moment offers a heartfelt look at her life beyond the baseball spotlight
articles.summary: MLB News: Kara Maxine Bieber is enjoying a season of change, but her latest style post shows that life is not only about becoming a mother of two. Five days ago.
articles.body: Kara Maxine Bieber is enjoying a season of change, but her latest style post shows that life is not only about becoming a mother of two. Five days ago, Shane Bieber’s wife shared a relaxed pre-fall look that felt simple and personal. With a flannel back in the mix, Kara leaned into an easy style that matched the mood of the season. The post also offered a small glimpse into her life away from the baseball field and the attention that comes with being married to a Blue Jays star.Kara Maxine Bieber’s easygoing look reflects the quieter, more personal moments taking shape in her lifeKara’s recent video was built around a simple idea. She called it her “pre-fall formula” and showed off an outfit that kept comfort and style in balance.The look featured a loose white top paired with dark bottoms. Sunglasses and a crossbody bag added a casual finish, while the flannel brought the fall touch she was clearly excited about.“The flannel is in the building & it feels good I can’t lie,” Kara wrote in the caption.There was nothing overly dressed up about the outfit. That may be what made the post stand out. It felt like a real snapshot of how Kara approaches everyday style.Her choice also fits the shift that comes with the changing season. Pre-fall fashion often sits between summer and cooler weather, and Kara’s look showed how a few simple pieces can make that transition feel easy.The timing makes the post even more meaningful. Kara is pregnant with her second child, giving this stage of her life a different feeling than it did when she became a first-time mother.Kara Maxine Bieber’s growing family makes this simple style moment part of a much bigger personal journeyKara and Shane Bieber announced in July that they were expecting their second child. Their son, Kav McClain Bieber, is now set to become a big brother.The couple welcomed Kav in March 2025, when Shane was still with the Cleveland Guardians. Since then, their family life has grown alongside Shane’s baseball career.Kara has also been open about how much family means to her. After announcing the pregnancy, she shared that nothing made her happier than building their family together.That makes her recent fashion post feel like more than another outfit video. It shows a woman enjoying the small parts of daily life while preparing for another major change at home.For many fans, Shane Bieber is known first through baseball. The 31-year-old pitcher is now with the Toronto Blue Jays and has built his career around the game.But Kara’s recent post offers a different view of the family behind the athlete.There is no game-day pressure in the video and no major family announcement. Instead, there is a flannel, a simple outfit and a woman enjoying a style choice that feels right for her.As Kara prepares to welcome another baby, moments like this offer a quieter look at the life she is building away from the baseball spotlight.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ketel Marte Reacts to Being Booed by D-Backs Fans After Viral Video from Pregame Press Conference
articles.summary: Arizona Diamondbacks star Ketel Marte said Tuesday night it was "a little strange" to make his return to Chase Field for the first time since his unexplained absence from an Aug. 17 game against the Boston Red Sox.
articles.body:
Arizona Diamondbacks star Ketel Marte said Tuesday night it was "a little strange" to make his return to Chase Field for the first time since his unexplained absence from an Aug. 17 game against the Boston Red Sox.

Marte, who was reinstated from the IL ahead of Monday's home game against the Philadelphia Phillies, was booed by fans in his first at-bat.

"I felt a little strange, in my first at-bat, but that's hopefully going to go away," Marte said through a Spanish language translator (h/t Arizona Sports' Alex Weiner).

Marte also addressed a pregame press conference in which he declined to share any message with Diamondbacks fans.

"When that question was made to me, I didn't really quite understand the word that was used at that moment," Marte said through his translator. "But I'm never going to stop loving my fans, and that's what I want them to understand."

Marte gave his postgame press conference while wearing a hat that read "May the bridges I burn light the way."

Marte previuosly told reporters at his pregame press conference he planned to apologize to his teammates.

"Thank God they accepted my apology," Marte said through his translator after the game. "Most important thing is for me to help them out, and most important thing is for me to stay healthy to be able to help this team."

Marte recorded one hit and a walk while batting fourth as designated hitter as the D-backs conceded a 2-1 loss in his return to the lineup.

Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo had indicated ahead of the game that he was concerned about the fan reception for Marte.

"I just want everyone to be patient with him, care for him and support him, because he feels the energy from people," Lovullo said.

Marte was initially placed on the restricted list when he failed to show up for the matchup against the Red Sox earlier this month.

He was later moved to the 10-day injured list because of inflammation in his left knee, according to Lovullo.

Marte said before the game through his translator his initial absence from the team had been the result of a "moment of frustration."

"I get along really well with Torey, and in that instance I failed him by not showing up," Marte said (h/t Arizona's Family's Nick King ). "That morning I woke up, my body was in pain, and I couldn't react. No one made the decision for me. I'm the one that made the decision to not show up."

He added he was now feeling "very well" both in terms of physical and mental health.

Marte is batting .250 with a .315 OBP, both of which would stand as the second-lowest full-season marks of his career, through 119 games this season.

More consistent production from Marte could be crucial to the Diamondbacks' hopes of making it back into the postseason. The club is sitting half a game back of the last NL Wild Card spot after Monday's loss to the Phillies.

articles.title: Yankees' Boone Explains Having Jazz Chisholm Jr. Steal Bases, Accepts Red Sox Broadcaster's Apology
articles.summary: New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone confirmed it was his decision to have Jazz Chisholm Jr. steal bases late in a six-run game last weekend, according to Greg Joyce of the New York Post.
articles.body:
New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone confirmed it was his decision to have Jazz Chisholm Jr. steal bases late in a six-run game last weekend, according to Greg Joyce of the New York Post.

Boone's comments came after Red Sox radio broadcaster Will Flemming called Chisholm a "bush league" player for stealing second and third base in the eighth inning of Sunday's 16-1 win over the Boston Red Sox.

ESPN's Michael Kay reported after the game Boone had confirmed over a phone call he told Chisholm to run.

Jazz Chisholm responds to Red Sox broadcaster's comments

"It was important to know that this came from me," Boone said, per Joyce. "I was not planning on running with that lead, had they played it straight. I was pretty animated and vocal with their dugout, just as far as, if they weren't going to play it straight, I wasn't just going to sit back. Absolutely not. I don't think they were going to not take their at-bats in the ninth inning.

"So I kind of object to some people saying, 'Well, that's waving the white flag.' So they weren't going to try to score in the ninth?"

Boone added he felt the Yankees had "done the right thing" and that he accepting Flemming's apology, according to Joyce.

Flemming expressed regret about his comments in a Monday post on social media.

Chisholm was among the multiple Yankees players who called Flemming out for his comments after the game.

Both Chisholm and Boone pushed back against the idea there were "unwritten rules" the Yankees had violated by stealing bases with a significant lead.

Boone said he respected "some" of these rules but felt they had "evolved," according to Joyce.

Chisholm initially got on base in the eighth by working a leadoff walk in five pitches from Red Sox pitcher Jovani Morán.

Kay originally reported Boone had said he would not have told Chisholm to run had the Red Sox held him at second base after the walk.

When he saw the Red Sox were not making an effort to stay close to Chisholm, Boone said he decided they were "playing real baseball" despite the six-run lead, according to Kay.

"They didn't hold me on, so I told Jazz to steal second," Kay said when recounting Boone's explanation. "And then, when he's on second, they're not even checking him. I said, 'You steal third'... If it was so important that you hold him on, why'd you bring the infield in when he's at third base?"

Chisholm was sent home on what turned out to be the first of two home runs from Austin Wells during a nine-run eighth inning.

The victory was an important one for the Yankees, which are heading into Tuesday with a three-game lead over the Red Sox for the top spot in the AL Wild Card race.

Should both clubs finish the season with the same record, the first tiebreaker would be their head-to-head record. Sunday's win allowed the Yankees to finish out the season series against the Red Sox with a 7-6 record.

articles.title: Stan Kroenke to Buy Angels for Reported MLB-Record Price, Rams Owner Now Controls 6 Pro Teams
articles.summary: Headed toward their 12th consecutive season without a playoff appearance, Arte Moreno's tenure as owner of the Los Angeles Angels is coming to an end.
articles.body:
Headed toward their 12th consecutive season without a playoff appearance, Arte Moreno's tenure as owner of the Los Angeles Angels is coming to an end.

Stan Kroenke, whose sports portfolio includes the NFL's Los Angeles Rams and NBA's Denver Nuggets, has entered into an agreement to purchase the Angels from Moreno through his Kroenke Sports & Entertainment company.

5 Things That Could Derail NYY Title Run 😱

Although the sale price has not been announced, it is expected to be a new MLB record that tops the $3.9 billion sale of the San Diego Padres, Bill Shaikin of the Los Angeles Times reports.

This deal comes almost exactly four years to the day that Moreno announced he was exploring a sale of the Angels before later ending that process to stay in control of the franchise.

In addition to the Rams and Nuggets, Kroenke's sports empire includes the Arsenal men's and women's teams, Colorado Avalanche, Colorado Rapids and Colorado Mammoth.

Kroenke's teams have combined to win nine championships, including two Super Bowls for the Rams, two Stanley Cup titles for the Avalanche, an NBA title for the Nuggets and the 2026 Premier League title for Arsenal.

When the sale becomes official, it will mark the end of Moreno's tumultuous tenure with the Angels. He originally purchased the franchise in May 2003 for $182.5 million from the Walt Disney Corporation.

Still boasting some of the key players from their 2002 World Series championship team, Moreno quickly made his presence felt by aggressively adding more talent to the mix.

Vladimir Guerrero and Bartolo Colón signed with the Angels as free agents after the 2003 season. Guerrero won AL MVP in his first year with the club. Colón won the AL Cy Young award in 2005.

The Angels made the playoffs five times in six years from 2004 to '09, reaching in the ALCS twice.

Since 2010, though, the Angels have made the playoffs once. They were swept in the ALDS by the Kansas City Royals in 2014. They currently own the second-longest active playoff drought among teams in the four major men's professional leagues, ahead of only the New York Jets.

The postseason drought overlaps with the most of Mike Trout's tenure (2011 to present) and the entirety of Shohei Ohtani's six-year run with the Angels (2018 to '23).

The Angels (53-85) are tied with the Athletics for last place in the AL West and the second-worst record in MLB overall. Their .384 winning percentage is on pace to be the worst in a single season in franchise history.

articles.title: MLB’s Los Angeles Angels to be sold to Rams, Arsenal owner Stan Kroenke
articles.summary: Kroenke Sports and Entertainment says it has reached a deal to purchase the Los Angeles Angels from Arte Moreno.
articles.body: Kroenke Sports and Entertainment says it has reached a deal to purchase the Los Angeles Angels from Arte Moreno. The company led by Stan Kroenke made the surprising announcement Tuesday, saying it expects to close the transaction in early 2027. Kroenke’s company owns the NFL’s Los Angeles Rams, Arsenal of the English Premier League, the NBA’s Denver Nuggets, the NHL’s Colorado Avalanche, Major League Soccer’s Colorado Rapids and SoFi Stadium, along with the large Hollywood Park campus around the multibillion-dollar Inglewood arena. The company has now added the Angels, whose turbulent 23-year tenure under Moreno’s ownership will finally come to an end. “The Angels are a storied franchise anchored in a great market,” Kroenke said in a statement. “We look forward to an exciting future with the Angels organization.” Moreno, an outdoor advertising magnate from Arizona, bought the Angels from the Walt Disney Company in 2003. While the club had steady success in its first years under Moreno with much of the roster that won the 2002 World Series, the Halos have entered a decline since winning their most recent playoff game in 2009. The Angels are currently headed to their 11th consecutive losing season and their 12th consecutive non-playoff season, both the longest active streaks in the majors. They’ve made the playoffs just once during the career of three-time AL MVP outfielder Mike Trout, who teamed with two-time AL MVP Shohei Ohtani for six straight seasons with no success. A significant portion of the Angels’ struggles can be attributed to the 80-year-old Moreno, who repeatedly inserted himself into personnel decisions. While he spent aggressively in his attempts to build a winner, his biggest moves usually backfired, with a series of high-profile acquisitions who produced a fraction of their anticipated impact. The Angels have also endured numerous troubles off the field during Moreno’s tenure, from the drug-related death of pitcher Tyler Skaggs to numerous smaller scandals. The Angels remained a healthy box office draw to their loyal Orange County fans during most of his tenure, but the fan base had lost patience in recent years. Angel Stadium’s slightly smaller crowds this season have regularly chanted “Sell the team!” The lack of success also began to wear on Moreno, whose children reportedly aren’t interested in carrying on in the baseball business. Moreno publicly explored a sale of the Angels in 2022, only to pull the team off the market in early 2023. “The Moreno family has been honored to steward the Angels for 23 years, and we believe with KSE’s experience and success, they are the best next owner for the franchise,” Moreno said in a statement. “The Angels organization looks forward to continuing its commitment to the fans, our employees, the players and our business partners.”

articles.title: Rams owner Stan Kroenke enters agreement to buy Angels from Arte Moreno for reported MLB record $4 billion
articles.summary: Stan Kroenke now has a hand in nearly every professional sports league.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Angels are the latest professional sports team to be sold in 2026. The Angels have been purchased by Los Angeles Rams owner Stan Kroenke, his company announced Tuesday.

The Angels confirmed the news Tuesday, with Kroenke saying the team has an "exciting future." Outgoing owner Arte Moreno also issued a statement, saying his family "has been honored to steward the Angels for 23 years."

The deal is expected to close early in 2027. Kroenke's company — Kroenke Sports & Entertainment — did not divulge how much Kroenke paid to take over the Angels. The team was valued at $2.8 billion by Forbes in March.

The Angels were reportedly purchased for an MLB record $4 billion , the The Athletic. The San Diego Padres, which sold earlier in 2026 , held the previous record at $3.9 billion .

The move sends yet another shockwave through the Los Angeles sports landscape, coming just weeks after Mark Walter sold the Los Angeles Lakers to a group led by Josh Kushner and Bob Iger.

In addition to those two teams, the Padres, Portland Trail Blazers and Seattle Seahawks have all changed ownership in 2026 .

The Arte Moreno era is over in Los Angeles

The decision to sell ends a mostly disappointing ownership tenure by Moreno, the first Latino majority owner in the sport. Moreno, 80, took over the Angels in 2003, when he purchased the franchise from the Walt Disney Company for $180 million.

Things started out positively, as the Angels — fresh off a World Series title — made the playoffs in five of the first seven years of Moreno's ownership. After a four-year drought, the team reached the postseason again in 2014, getting swept in the first round. The Angels haven't made the playoffs since then, the longest active postseason drought in the sport.

While Moreno always showed a willingness to spend, his penchant for buying stars often backfired. Vladimir Guerrero, whom the team signed ahead of the 2004 MLB season, had a successful second half of his career with the franchise. But future free-agent splurges — like Albert Pujols, Josh Hamilton and Anthony Rendon — failed to live up to their former luster, often leaving the franchise in a rough financial spot.

All of those signings happened to overlap with perhaps the biggest win — and failure — of Moreno's ownership tenure. The Angels drafted Mike Trout in 2009, promoted him to the majors in 2011 and proceeded to have eight straight seasons in which he was arguably the best player in the majors. Despite Trout's excellence, the team made the postseason just once during his stardom, when it was swept in 2014.

As Trout started to slow down, the team managed to convince two-way star Shohei Ohtani to sign with the Angels. Despite the presence of both players, the Angels never made the postseason with the pair. Moreno ultimately couldn't re-sign Ohtani in 2023, paving the way for him to join the Los Angeles Dodgers, where he immediately won two straight World Series.

Stan Kroenke continues to buy sports teams

The name Stan Kroenke should sound pretty familiar in the professional sports realm. On top of owning the Rams, Kroenke also holds ownership stakes in the Denver Nuggets, Colorado Avalanche, Colorado Rapids and Colorado Mammoth — a professional lacrosse team.

He's had plenty of success with those franchises, winning two Super Bowls with the Rams (one as a majority owner, one as a minority partner), two Stanley Cups with the Avalanche, one NBA championship with the Nuggets and an MLS Cup with the Rapids. He's an MLB title away from owning the sports equivalent of Thanos' Infinity Gauntlet.

Getting the Angels back to championship level won't be easy. The franchise has not experienced a winning season since 2015. There's some young talent on the roster — Zach Neto and Nolan Schanuel on the hitting side and Reid Detmers and Walbert Ureña in the rotation — but the team still seems far off from competing again … even with Trout turning in his best year since 2022.

Some of the team's stumbles along the way have been attributed to Moreno, who reportedly played a major role in the team signing some of those bad contracts and received criticism for the upkeep of team facilities .

If Kroenke is willing to invest in upgrades that meaningfully improve those facilities and stay out of the way when it comes to personnel moves, that might be enough to get the Angels back on the right track. Kroenke has shown an ability to do that with his other teams, so it might not be that long before the Angels are taken seriously again.

Arsenal owner Stan Kroenke has bought Major League Baseball franchise the Los Angeles Angels in a deal reportedly worth $4bn.

Kroenke, who has had a controlling stake in Arsenal since 2011, now owns teams in six major sporting leagues.

The Angels join NFL side the Los Angeles Rams, the NBA's Denver Nuggets, the Colorado Avalanche of the NHL and MLS team the Colorado Rapids, as well as the Gunners, in being under the 79-year-old's control.

While the cost of the deal was not announced, the Los Angeles Times , external have reported that it is a record price for an MLB team, exceeding the $3.9bn the San Diego Padres were sold for in August.

"The Angels are a storied franchise anchored in a great market," Kroenke said in a statement.

"We look forward to an exciting future with the Angels organisation."

Previous owner Arte Moreno bought the Angels in 2003 but had come under pressure from fans to sell the club after 11 years without qualifying for the play-offs.

With less than a month of the regular season remaining, that is set to extend to 12 seasons - the longest active play-off drought in the MLB - with the Angels holding the joint-worst record in the American League.

Fan discontent has intensified this season with their "Tarps Off" protest, in which supporters went shirtless and waved their shirts above their heads, going viral.

Chants of "sell the team" and "we want play-offs" have also been heard regularly at Angel Stadium.

A statement from Moreno read: "The Moreno family has been honoured to steward the Angels for 23 years and we believe with [Kroenke's holding company] Kroenke Sports & Entertainment's experience and success, they are the best next owner for the franchise."
